pages.title: Access Requests
pages.description: Review and fulfill elevated access and asset requests from the universal approval inbox.
headings: Granting doors, not inventing a second HR file
pages.content: Access Requests — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Access Requests Elevated access inbox Granting doors, not inventing a second HR file Access and asset requests land here so an administrator can fulfill a laptop, badge, or elevated permission from the same universal approval family as leave and timesheet. Admin → Access requests Route /admin/access-requests Org flag accessRequestsEnabled Requester (employee) · HR Admin / Org Admin fulfill The job of this console Review pending requests, fulfill or reject against Employee and asset masters, and close the row so the trail stays on the approval domain. Export only when audit wants a snapshot. Seat at the table Anyone may raise a request when the flag is on. Fulfillment is for HR Admin and Org Admin. Managers see team items in My Approvals, not this admin register. The working rhythm Filter by status, open a row, fulfill against source records, confirm it closes. Do not create a side spreadsheet of laptops — assets stay on the People assets register. Moments that bring you here New joiner hardware. Production-admin for an incident. Contractor access that should expire. After offboarding, leftover grants still open. ⓘ Fulfillment writes to source records Closing a request does not create a parallel asset ledger. Employee and asset masters remain the source; this console only routes the decision. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Access requests] --> B[Filter pending] B --> C[Open a request] C --> D{Justified?} D -->|Yes| E[Approve / fulfill] D -->|No| F[Deny with reason] E --> G[Grant recorded] F --> G 1 Open the register Admin → Access requests. 2 Filter pending Status chips show what still needs a decision. 3 Review Check persona, asset, and justification. 4 Decide Approve to fulfill or deny with a reason. Overview Access requests are a domain of the universal approval engine. Fulfillment writes to existing people/asset records — this page is not an independent permission store. How to use 1. Search before paging Actor, asset, and headline search is faster than scrolling. 2. Deny with a reason Empty denials create follow-up noise. 3. Check related policies Some grants still need Roles & permissions after fulfillment. Related pages Roles & permissions What the grant actually unlocks. Approval policies SLA for ASSET_ACCESS. Audit Fulfillment events. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: API Keys
pages.description: Issue, export metadata, and revoke integration keys. Secret material is shown once.
headings: Issue, copy once, revoke without ceremony
pages.content: API Keys — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → API Keys Integration credentials Issue, copy once, revoke without ceremony API keys are integration credentials. Secret material is shown once. Metadata — name, last used, status — is what you export and audit. Admin → Developer portal → API keys Route /admin/api-keys Org flag apiKeysEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin · integration owner The job of this console Issue a key for a named app, copy the secret immediately, then revoke when the partner rotates or leaves. Never paste keys into tickets or Work Graph comments. Seat at the table The same administrators who own the developer portal. Engineers outside Admin should request a key, not share an existing one. The working rhythm Open keys, issue, copy, confirm the partner can call, then close the reveal. Revoke on incident. Export metadata for change control, not the secret. Moments that bring you here New integration. Scheduled rotation. A key seen in a screenshot. After an employee who held the secret leaves. ⓘ Metadata only after the first reveal Audit and export never include the raw secret. Treat a lost secret as compromised — revoke rather than search logs. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open API keys] --> B[Create key] B --> C[Copy secret once] C --> D[Store in vault] D --> E[Use from integration] E --> F[Revoke when done] 1 Open API keys Developer hub → API keys. 2 Create Name, app, and expiry. 3 Copy once The secret is not shown again. 4 Revoke Immediately on leak or owner change. Overview Keys authenticate against existing v2 APIs. They are not a second permission model — RBAC and persona masking still apply. How to use 1. Never commit secrets Docs and tickets get the key id only. 2. Export is metadata CSV does not include secrets. 3. Short expiry for pilots Rotate before go-live. Related pages Developer portal App registry. Webhooks Push instead of poll. Masking policy What API responses hide. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Approval Policies
pages.description: Routing rules, SLA hours, escalation, and simulation for leave, timesheet, attendance, and related domains.
headings: Who must say yes, and how long they have
pages.content: Approval Policies — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Approval Policies Routing and SLA Who must say yes, and how long they have Approval policies are the routing rules, SLA hours, escalation, and simulation for leave, timesheet, attendance, and related domains. The universal inbox only shows work these policies created. Admin → Approval policies Route /admin/approval-policies Org flag approvalPoliciesEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Publish a domain policy so requests find the right manager chain, expire with an SLA, and escalate when silent. Simulate a sample request before publish. Pause or revise a policy without rewriting the approval engine. Seat at the table HR and org administrators. Managers act on My Approvals; they do not author policies here. Employees never see this console. The working rhythm Filter by domain, create or edit levels, set SLA and escalation, simulate, then publish. Revisit after an org restructure so manager chains still resolve. Use delegation when a person is out — do not clone a whole policy for one absence. Moments that bring you here A new leave type needs a two-step chain. Timesheet SLA is too loose before payroll lock. Escalation never fired because the manager field was empty. After org-structure changes, to re-simulate. ⓘ Policies route; they do not store the request Leave, timesheet, and attendance records stay on their source tables. This console only decides the path. Authority still comes from ApprovalAuthorityService. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Approval policies] --> B[Filter by domain] B --> C[Create or edit policy] C --> D[Set levels / SLA / escalation] D --> E[Simulate] E --> F{Looks right?} F -->|No| C F -->|Yes| G[Save / publish] G --> H[Live approvals use policy] 1 Open the console Admin → Approval policies. 2 Pick a domain Leave, timesheet, attendance, or other routed types. 3 Configure routing Approver levels, SLA hours, reminders, auto-escalate. 4 Simulate Run a sample payload before publishing. 5 Publish Workspace approvals pick up the saved policy. Overview Policies are workflow configuration — they do not replace domain records. Timesheet chain behavior may also require Work-Time Governance admin.policyManagement. How to use 1. Simulate before publish Use the simulation panel with a realistic requester and amount. 2. Keep SLA and escalation paired Escalation hours should exceed SLA hours. 3. Draft vs published Draft policies do not route live work. 4. Link delegation Acting managers are configured on Delegation rules, not inside the policy JSON. Related pages Delegation rules Acting managers for the same domains. My Approvals Inbox that consumes these policies. Feature flags Work-Time Governance policy-management gate. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Audit & Compliance
pages.description: Organization-wide audit event register and timeline — who did what, when, on which record.
headings: The org-wide register of meaningful actions
pages.content: Audit & Compliance — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Audit Who did what, when The org-wide register of meaningful actions Audit & compliance is the organization-wide event register and timeline — who did what, when, on which record — across admin, people, and delivery activity the product already records. Admin → Audit & compliance Route /admin/audit Org flag auditEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Find an event, open the timeline, and export when an auditor asks. Filter by actor, record, and window. This is investigation, not a place to undo a change. Seat at the table Administrators and compliance operators. Employees do not get an org-wide audit. Sensitive fields stay masked according to persona policy. The working rhythm Set a window, filter, open a row, follow the record link into the owning console if you need to correct data there. Use compliance export when the ask is a pack, not a single event. Moments that bring you here Someone changed a flag and menus vanished. A leave balance looks rewritten. An auditor wants last quarter’s admin actions. After a suspected privilege change. ⓘ Masked summaries for sensitive fields Salary, bank, tax, and similar values are not stored raw in audit snippets when persona masking applies. Follow the security console for the masking policy itself. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Audit] --> B[Scan KPI / volume] B --> C[Search actor or entity] C --> D[Register or timeline] D --> E[Open event] E --> F[Export CSV if required] 1 Open Audit Admin → Audit & compliance. 2 Search first Actor, action, entity, or headline. 3 Switch view Register for scanning, timeline for day grouping. 4 Export CSV is for evidence — still masked where policy requires. Overview This console is the admin register over the unified audit stream. Entity screens (project, profile, leave) show the same events in context — see the HRMS Unified Audit Trail guide. How to use 1. Writes are best-effort Audit never blocks a save or approval. 2. No legacy backfill History starts when audit writes were enabled. 3. Delegate vs actor Delegation actions record both parties. Related pages Unified Audit Trail Entity-level timeline. Approval policies Decisions that generate events. Admin dashboard Volume KPIs that drill here. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Automation Rules
pages.description: Build trigger → condition → action graphs, save drafts, then publish from the studio.
headings: Trigger, condition, action — drafts stay silent
pages.content: Automation Rules — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Rule Builder Graph editor Trigger, condition, action — drafts stay silent Automation rules is the graph editor: trigger → condition → action. Save drafts, then publish from the studio. A draft never fires against live events. Admin → Workflow automation → Rule builder Route /admin/automation-rules Org flag automationRulesEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Build or edit the graph, keep a draft until the path is right, then return to the studio to publish. Pause a live rule in the studio before you reshape it here. Seat at the table The same administrators who own Workflow studio. Contributors do not get a builder. Partners should not receive export of graphs with production URLs without review. The working rhythm Open a rule, edit trigger and conditions, attach actions (notify, route, connector), save draft, publish from the studio. Use notification templates for copy. Moments that bring you here A new leave type needs a follow-on mail. An SLA breach should open a ticket. After a connector change. When a published graph mis-routes and must be paused first. ⓘ Studio publishes; builder structures This page does not replace Workflow studio as the operations desk. Notification copy still comes from notification templates. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Rule builder] --> B[Select trigger] B --> C[Add conditions] C --> D[Add actions] D --> E[Save draft] E --> F[Publish] F --> G[Studio shows live] 1 Open Rule builder Admin → Workflow automation → Rule builder. 2 Trigger Domain event the rule listens to. 3 Conditions & actions Keep graphs small and testable. 4 Save then publish Drafts do not fire. Overview The builder writes workflow configuration records. Actions must call approved canonical services — never a disconnected table. How to use 1. One trigger per rule Split complex graphs. 2. Test with a sandbox event Publish only after a dry run. 3. Studio for ops Pause/resume without opening the builder. Related pages Workflow studio Publish and pause. Developer portal Outbound webhooks as actions. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Compliance Export
pages.description: Pack readiness and exportable evidence for audits — composed from live source entities.
pages.content: Compliance Export — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Compliance Export Evidence pack Readiness composed from live entities Compliance export packs readiness and exportable evidence for audits — composed from live source entities, not a warehouse you curate by hand. Admin → Compliance export Route /admin/compliance-export Org flag complianceExportEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console See which evidence families are ready, run an export, and hand the pack to audit. Fix gaps in the owning consoles (retention, audit, policies), then re-export. Do not edit the pack as if it were a source. Seat at the table Administrators preparing an audit. External auditors receive the file; they do not open this console. The working rhythm Read readiness, close gaps on source consoles, export, store the file in the audit binder. Repeat when the window changes. Moments that bring you here SOC or customer security questionnaire. Year-end. After a retention hold. When a previous pack is stale because flags or policies changed. ⓘ Export is a snapshot The pack is not a second system of record. If a number looks wrong, fix Employee, policy, or audit at source and export again. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Compliance export] --> B[Review pack readiness] B --> C[Select a pack] C --> D[Generate export] D --> E[Download] E --> F[Retain with auditor] 1 Open Compliance export Admin → Compliance export. 2 Readiness Missing source data shows as incomplete packs. 3 Generate Export uses live Employee, audit, and related sources. 4 Store externally The pack is evidence, not a new system of record. Overview Packs compose from canonical services. Persona masking still applies — do not unmask salary or bank data in the file. How to use 1. Fix readiness first Incomplete packs usually mean flags or retention gaps. 2. Masking still applies Exports honor Security masking policy. 3. Audit the download Treat the file as sensitive. Related pages Audit & compliance Event evidence. Data retention What still exists to export. Masking policy What the pack may reveal. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Admin Dashboard
pages.description: Control-tower view of audit activity, access health, compliance readiness, and flag adoption for administrators.
headings: Health of the org, not a second analytics product
pages.content: Admin Dashboard — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Dashboard Control tower Health of the org, not a second analytics product The admin dashboard is a control-tower slice of audit activity, access health, compliance readiness, and flag adoption. Charts here are composed from the same events and flags the other consoles already own. Admin → Admin dashboard Route /admin/dashboard Org flag dashboardEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console See whether governance is drifting — failed jobs, pending access, stale flags, thin audit coverage — then jump into the owning console. This page does not approve leave, edit roles, or toggle flags; it points. Seat at the table Administrators whose persona can open Admin. Managers use People and Workspace dashboards instead. Finance and project personas stay on their own towers. The working rhythm Open the tower, read the insight strip, drill a card into audit, flags, or jobs, act there, then return to confirm the signal cleared. Refresh when you have just published a flag or retention hold. Moments that bring you here Monday ops scan. After enabling a high-risk flag. When compliance asks if the org is ready for an evidence pack. After a job failure email. Not for workforce headcount — that lives on the People dashboard. ⓘ Read model of live consoles Cards are assembled from audit, access, flags, and jobs. Do not treat a dashboard number as a ledger you can edit. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Admin dashboard] --> B[Scan KPI strip] B --> C{Spikes?} C -->|Audit / denials| D[Drill charts] C -->|Pending access| E[Access requests] C -->|Flags / compliance| F[App config] D --> G[Investigate audit trail] E --> G F --> H[Application Config] 1 Open Admin dashboard Admin → Admin dashboard. 2 Scan KPI strip Audit events, denials, pending access, compliance %, flag adoption. 3 Drill charts Use volume and denial charts to spot anomalies. 4 Follow up Jump to audit, access requests, or Application Config as needed. Overview The Admin Dashboard aggregates operational signals — it does not replace module-specific registers. Use it to decide where to dig next. How to use 1. Confirm access Requires admin insights / dashboard flags and an admin persona. 2. Refresh after changes After enabling flags or resolving access requests, refresh the snapshot. 3. Link out for action Charts inform; actual remediation happens on audit, roles, or app config pages. Related pages Application Config Flags and org structure. Notification templates Outbound message templates. Audit Trail Event detail for investigations. Admin & Access RBAC overview chapter. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Data Retention
pages.description: Retention schedules, purge windows, and compliance holds for operational records.
headings: Schedules and legal holds on operational records
pages.content: Data Retention — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Data Retention Keep, hold, purge Schedules and legal holds on operational records Data retention is the schedule of keep windows, purge eligibility, and compliance holds for operational records. A hold freezes purge; it does not freeze the live business record from legitimate edits. Admin → Data retention Route /admin/data-retention Org flag dataRetentionEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Publish retention for each family, place a hold when legal asks, and understand what purge will touch before it runs. Coordinate with jobs that actually execute purge. Seat at the table Administrators with compliance duty. Employees never set their own retention. Developers do not add ad-hoc deletes that bypass these windows. The working rhythm Open a family, set the window, save, place or lift a hold, then confirm scheduled jobs. Spot-check audit after a purge window elapses. Moments that bring you here A litigation hold. GDPR-style deletion request that still must respect a hold. After a new module starts writing records with no schedule. Year-end policy review. ⓘ Holds beat purge A compliance hold keeps records even when the calendar says they are eligible. Jobs honor this console; do not script around it. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Data retention] --> B[Select a schedule] B --> C[Set window / hold] C --> D[Save] D --> E[Jobs honor schedule] E --> F[Audit the change] 1 Open Data retention Admin → Data retention. 2 Select a family Timesheet, audit, documents, and related records. 3 Set window Retention days plus optional legal hold. 4 Confirm jobs Scheduled jobs execute purge — do not delete by hand. Overview Retention is policy over existing source tables. It does not introduce a parallel archive of business truth. How to use 1. Legal holds first Holds block purge even when the window elapsed. 2. Pair with compliance export Export evidence before shortening a window. 3. Do not purge production blindly Preview job impact on Scheduled jobs. Related pages Compliance export Evidence packs before purge. Scheduled jobs Purge runners. Masking policy Access while records still exist. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Delegation Rules
pages.description: Outgoing delegates and managers you are acting for — scoped to attendance, timesheet, and leave.
headings: Coverage for attendance, timesheet, and leave — not a standing proxy
pages.content: Delegation Rules — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Delegation Acting for someone else Coverage for attendance, timesheet, and leave — not a standing proxy Delegation rules name outgoing delegates and the managers you are acting for, scoped to attendance, timesheet, and leave. A delegate sees those items in My Approvals for the window you set. Admin → Delegation rules Route /admin/delegation Org flag delegationEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin · Manager (own outgoing) The job of this console Record who covers whom, for which domain, and until when. Stop a delegate the day the manager returns. Do not use this as a permanent second manager — that belongs in org structure. Seat at the table Administrators configure org-wide patterns. Managers typically set their own outgoing delegate. Employees do not delegate approval authority from this console. The working rhythm Open the register, add an outgoing delegate or an acting-for row, pick domains, set dates, save. Confirm the delegate sees the inbox. End the row when coverage stops. Moments that bring you here Leave of a people manager. End-of-year freeze when approvers travel. A new skip-level who should not inherit every domain. After mistaken standing proxies, to unwind them. ⓘ Delegation rides on ApprovalAuthority This is not a parallel approval engine. Live requests still follow published policies; the delegate is a temporary actor on that path. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Delegation rules] --> B[Review outgoing / acting tabs] B --> C[Add delegate] C --> D[Set scope + dates] D --> E[Save] E --> F[Delegate sees inbox] F --> G[Audit records actor vs delegate] 1 Open Delegation Admin → Delegation rules. 2 Choose tab Outgoing delegates vs managers you are acting for. 3 Set scope Attendance, timesheet, leave — plus duration. 4 Verify inbox Delegate sees items in My Approvals for the window. Overview Delegation is a workflow overlay on ApprovalAuthorityService. It does not rewrite the underlying timesheet, leave, or attendance records. How to use 1. Keep windows short Open-ended delegates are hard to audit. 2. Match policy domains A leave-only delegate cannot approve timesheets. 3. Check acting calendar Overlaps are visible on the calendar panel. 4. Confirm after login Delegates may need a refresh to see the acting banner. Related pages Approval policies Routing that delegates execute. My Approvals Delegate inbox. Audit & compliance Actor vs delegate on events. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Developer Portal
pages.description: Register apps, review usage, then manage API keys and webhooks from the same hub.
headings: Apps, keys, and webhooks from one door
pages.content: Developer Portal — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Developer Portal Extensibility hub Apps, keys, and webhooks from one door The developer portal is where you register apps, review usage, then manage API keys and webhooks. It is the hub; the key and webhook registers are the sharp tools. Admin → Developer portal Route /admin/developer Org flag developerPortalOverviewEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin · integration owner The job of this console Register an app, understand usage, then issue keys or subscribe webhooks without scattering credentials in chat. Revoke from the same hub when an integration leaves. Seat at the table Administrators and named integration owners. Ordinary employees do not open the portal. External vendors receive credentials once, not a login to this console. The working rhythm Open the hub, add or select an app, jump to API keys or webhooks, complete the issue or subscription, store the secret offline. Review usage when a partner says they are throttled. Moments that bring you here First connector. A vendor rotation of secrets. After a leaked key. When webhook delivery failures pile up. ⓘ Secrets are shown once The portal stores metadata, not a recoverable plaintext vault. If a secret is lost, revoke and issue again. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Developer portal] --> B[Register app] B --> C[Issue API key] C --> D[Optional webhook] D --> E[Monitor usage] 1 Open portal Admin → Developer portal. 2 Register app Name, owner, and scopes. 3 Keys & webhooks Hub tabs for day-two operations. 4 Watch usage Revoke unused keys. Overview Extensibility is gated by developer flags. Tokens must not be pasted into docs or AI logs. How to use 1. Least privilege scopes Do not issue blanket admin keys. 2. Rotate regularly Revoke on owner change. 3. Hub tabs API keys and Webhooks are sibling consoles. Related pages API keys Issue and revoke. Webhooks Outbound event delivery. Audit Key create/revoke events. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Feature Flags
pages.description: Stage pilots, track adoption, and govern high-risk toggles — including the Work-Time Governance catalog on the same console.
headings: Turn surfaces on without shipping a build
1 — Toggle a flag for a pilot
pages.content: Feature Flags — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Feature Flags Pilot and catalog control Turn surfaces on without shipping a build Feature flags are the live catalog of org toggles, including Work-Time Governance families on the same console. A flag change is how a pilot sees a menu tomorrow without a deploy — and how you take it back just as fast. Admin → Feature flags Route /admin/feature-flags Org flag featureFlagsEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Stage a pilot, watch adoption, and govern high-risk toggles. Enable for an org unit before global on. Read dependents so a child never appears while its parent is off. Use the Work-Time Governance panel for timesheet, approval, and attendance catalog families — not a separate route. Seat at the table Only administrators who can open Admin and whose org has featureFlagsEnabled. Contributors never see this register. Persona navigation still decides who sees a page after the flag is on. The working rhythm Filter by module and status, open a flag, enable for a pilot, save, then log in as a test persona and confirm menus. Rollback by disabling. Coordinate Application Config keys and role permissions when a flag alone is not enough. Moments that bring you here A new module is ready for one country. Work-time rules must go live before payroll lock. A flag caused a bad menu and needs an immediate off. Before go-live, to confirm dependents are unblocked. ⓘ Flags gate menus; they are not Application Config Lists, calendars, and master values still live in Application Config. Roles still decide who may open a gated page. Turn the flag on, then finish config and persona access. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Feature flags] --> B[Filter by module/status] B --> C[Select a flag] C --> D[Enable for pilot / org] D --> E[Save] E --> F[Verify test persona menus] F --> G{Issues?} G -->|Yes| H[Disable / rollback] G -->|No| I[Monitor adoption] 1 Open Feature flags Admin → Feature flags. 2 Filter Module and status chips narrow the register. 3 Change state Enable for a pilot org unit or globally. 4 Verify Log in as a test persona and confirm menus appear. 5 Rollback if needed Disable the flag without a deploy. Overview This console is the live catalog of org feature flags. The Work-Time Governance panel on the same page turns catalog families on or off in Application Config — it is not a separate route. How to use 1. Prefer pilots before global on High-risk flags should ship to a pilot org unit first. 2. Read dependents Blocked children stay off until the parent flag is enabled. 3. Coordinate with config Some flags still need Application Config keys or role permissions. 4. Use Work-Time Governance for time rules Approval chain, timesheet validation, and attendance catalog live in the WTG panel below the register. Related pages Roles & permissions Menu access for flag admin. Application Config Org overrides that flags often gate. Work-Time Governance Catalog families managed from this page. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

headings: Every admin console, one door from the Guide button
pages.content: Admin consoles — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin Governance map Every admin console, one door from the Guide button This hub is the table of contents for governance screens — flags, roles, policies, audit, jobs, and extensibility. It is not a live console. Each in-app Guide button opens the matching page listed here, not this index, unless the route only has the /admin fallback. Docs · Admin consoles Route /admin/* HR Admin · Org Admin · anyone implementing Tracopus The job of this console Orient an administrator to the right how-to before they touch live org data. Scan the list, open the screen that matches the menu they are about to use, and follow that page’s flowcharts instead of guessing across modules. Seat at the table Written for people who can open Admin in the product, plus implementation partners setting an org for the first time. Employees and managers do not need this hub for day-to-day work. The working rhythm Start here only when you do not know which console owns the change. Pick a screen, read its briefing, then work in the app with the Guide button as a spare copy of the same page. Moments that bring you here Day-one setup. A new HR admin asking where flags live versus Application Config. After a release, when a menu moved under Admin. Never as a substitute for the live register. ⓘ Hub, not a source of truth Nothing on this index writes Employee, Project, or Application Config. Follow each console’s own note for what it is allowed to change. How to use these guides From any Admin screen, the book icon in the page hero opens the how-to for that route. Leave-admin screens (policies, test lab, calendars) live with the HRMS leave guides because they share those source services. Application Config org.json + role.json. Notification templates Email and in-app copy. Audit & compliance Org event register. System errors Ops inbox for SF / ZingHR / health. Masking policy Persona field grants. Data retention Schedules and holds. Compliance export Evidence packs. Payroll readiness Mandatory gates. Shift policies Working-day calendars. pages.title: Industry Templates
pages.description: Apply a packaged industry template to seed Application Config lists, flags, and related setup — review the diff before apply.
headings: A diff you review before it touches config
pages.content: Industry Templates — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Industry Templates Packaged seed A diff you review before it touches config Industry templates seed Application Config lists, flags, and related setup from a packaged industry. Apply is a reviewed diff, not an invisible overwrite. Admin → Industry templates Route /admin/industry-templates Org flag appconfigEnabled Org Admin The job of this console Pick a template, read the diff against current org config, apply only what you intend, then verify lists and flags in Application Config and Feature flags. Never apply blindly on a production org that already has local lists. Seat at the table Org administrators. HR admins may be asked to review the diff; they should not treat this as a daily console. The working rhythm Open templates, choose an industry, review added and replaced keys, apply, then spot-check Application Config and a test persona menu. Moments that bring you here Greenfield tenant. A new line of business that matches a pack. After a sandbox reset. Not for a one-field list edit — that belongs in Application Config. ⓘ Templates seed Application Config The template is not a lasting source of truth. After apply, org.json / Application Config owns the values. Review the diff every time. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Industry templates] --> B[Select a pack] B --> C[Review detail] C --> D[Apply preview] D --> E{Accept writes?} E -->|No| C E -->|Yes| F[Apply] F --> G[Verify App Config] 1 Browse packs Admin → Industry templates. 2 Open detail See which config keys and lists the pack touches. 3 Apply flow Confirm the write target, then apply. 4 Verify Open Application Config and spot-check lists/flags. Overview Templates write into Application Config and related source entities. They are not an independent industry database. How to use 1. Read the diff Never apply blind on a production org. 2. One pack at a time Overlapping packs can clobber lists. 3. Checklist first Finish day-one checklist items that templates assume exist. Related pages Setup checklist Manual day-one items. Application Config Where packs write. Feature flags Flags templates may enable. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Scheduled Jobs
pages.description: ScheduleType inventory with last-run status and manual Run now / Run scan.
headings: Last run, next run, and a careful Run now
pages.content: Scheduled Jobs — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Scheduled Jobs Scheduled work Last run, next run, and a careful Run now Scheduled jobs are the ScheduleType inventory with last-run status and manual Run now / Run scan. Accruals, reminders, and scans live here; they are not started from a hidden cron UI. Admin → Scheduled jobs (deep link) Route /admin/jobs HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console See what is failing, trigger a safe manual run when operations need it, and leave timing to the schedule. Do not hammer Run now on payroll-adjacent jobs without knowing the window. Seat at the table Administrators and support engineers. Employees never run jobs. Developers still own job code; this is operations, not a code editor. The working rhythm Scan last-run status, open a failing type, read the error, fix source data or config, then Run now if the job is idempotent enough. Export only for incident notes. Moments that bring you here Leave accrual did not fire. A reminder storm. After a flag change that a job gates. Overnight failure in the admin dashboard job card. ⓘ Jobs mutate source records on purpose A run writes to the domain it serves (balances, notifications, scans). Treat Run now as a production action, not a refresh button. Overview Jobs operate on existing domain tables (timesheet lock, leave accrual, retention purge). This page is an operations console, not a new scheduler database. How to use 1. Do not hammer Run now Overlapping runs can lock rows. 2. Read the type name ScheduleType maps to a known backend job. 3. Failed runs Fix data or flags before retrying. Prefer overrides over forks Adjust the existing event template when possible so keys stay aligned with the backend. 2. It does not invent a vault; it decides what each persona sees on existing screens. Admin → Security settings Route /admin/security Org flag securityEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Set which personas see which sensitive fields, confirm Employee 360 and payroll screens honor the policy, and keep AI / work-graph snippets on masked summaries. Change policy here, not by forking page code. Seat at the table Org and HR administrators. Payroll managers still need the payroll flag and persona; masking is additional. Employees should never see others’ bank fields because a flag was left open. The working rhythm Open the policy, adjust a persona’s field set, save, then view the same employee as that persona. Recheck analytics and AI audit logs for raw values. Moments that bring you here A new finance persona. An auditor asking who can see compensation. After an AI feature ships that might echo salary. When a screenshot leaked a bank field. ⓘ Masking is not encryption at rest Source tables still hold the values. This console governs presentation and derived snippets. Do not persist unmasked sensitive fields in AI audit or graph metadata. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Security] --> B[Pick a field] B --> C[Set persona grants] C --> D[Save] D --> E[Employee 360 / exports honor policy] E --> F[Audit when writes enabled] 1 Open Security settings Admin → Security settings. 2 Select a field Registry lists sensitive attributes. 3 Set grants VISIBLE, MASKED, or HIDDEN per persona. 4 Verify Open Employee 360 as a restricted persona. Overview Masking is evaluated with PersonaContextService. AI audits and Work Graph must store masked summaries only — never raw salary, bank, tax, or medical values. How to use 1. Default to MASKED VISIBLE should be rare outside Payroll / HR Admin. 2. Export gates Some rules also restrict CSV/PDF export. 3. Pair with retention Hidden fields may still exist until Data retention purges them. Related pages Data retention Purge windows for the same fields. Audit Who viewed or exported sensitive data. pages.title: System errors
pages.description: Ops inbox for Salesforce, ZingHR, credentials, schedulers, health, and leave integration failures — with clear cause and next steps.
headings: Why Salesforce, ZingHR, or health failed — and what to do
pages.content: System errors — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → System errors Ops inbox Why Salesforce, ZingHR, or health failed — and what to do System errors is the role-gated ops inbox for integration and platform failures — Salesforce, ZingHR, credential reload, schedulers, host health, and leave-integration DLQ — with human-readable cause and a suggested next step. Admin → System errors Route /admin/system-errors Org flag systemErrorsEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Scan open and critical failures, open a row for Why this failed and What to do, follow the deep link to Connections or Jobs, then Acknowledge or Mark resolved after you fix the root cause. This is an operator ledger, not a second source of truth. Seat at the table ADMIN and HR_ADMIN personas. Enabled by default; set adminModules.systemErrorsEnabled to false on a role to hide it. Org can turn the master off with systemErrorsAdminEnabled . The working rhythm Filter by status and source → open a row → read summary and suggested action → fix credentials or retry the job → Acknowledge or Resolve. Repeat when the same fingerprint bumps occurrence count. Moments that bring you here PO import stuck after Salesforce auth failure. Leave sync quiet while ZingHR is down. Connections health red. Secrets file write failed on reload. Scheduler catch for SALESFORCE or ZINGHR_LEAVES. ⓘ Ledger, not the owning system Sync logs, health probes, and leave DLQ remain the technical sources. System Errors stores masked context only — never passwords or tokens. Fix the owning console (Connections, Jobs, Leave integrations), then resolve the event here. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open System errors] --> B[Scan Open / Critical KPIs] B --> C[Filter source or status] C --> D[Open a row] D --> E[Read Why / What to do] E --> F[Fix Connections or Jobs] F --> G[Acknowledge or Resolve] 1 Open System errors Admin → System errors. 2 Scan KPIs Open, Critical, and Last 24h set the priority. 3 Filter Status and source chips narrow the register. 4 Read the drawer Why this failed plus suggested action and deep link. 5 Fix and close Update credentials or retry, then Acknowledge / Resolve. Overview This console is the operator-facing ledger over integration and platform failures. Events dedupe by fingerprint (occurrence count bumps on repeat). Sync logs, health probes, and leave DLQ remain the technical sources — System Errors stores masked summaries and suggested actions only. How to use 1. Default on; role can disable Unset role flags stay enabled. Set adminModules.systemErrorsEnabled to false to hide the menu for a role. 2. Never store secrets detail_json is sanitized — passwords and tokens are masked. 3. Fix the owner first Use the deep link to Connections, Jobs, or leave integrations, then resolve the event. 4. Acknowledge vs resolve Acknowledge means you are working it; Resolve means the failure is handled. Related pages Connections Update Salesforce / ZingHR credentials. Scheduled jobs Retry SF / ZingHR schedule types. Audit & compliance Org-wide who-did-what register. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Webhooks

headings: Subscribe, inspect deliveries, retry a miss
pages.content: Webhooks — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Webhooks Outbound events Subscribe, inspect deliveries, retry a miss Webhooks subscribe to domain events, show delivery attempts, and retry failures. They push what already happened on Employee, leave, ticket, and similar records. Admin → Developer portal → Webhooks Route /admin/webhooks Org flag webhooksEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin · integration owner The job of this console Subscribe an endpoint, verify signatures on the partner side, watch deliveries, and retry a failed batch. Pause or delete a subscription that is flooding a dead URL. Seat at the table Integration owners with Admin access. Endpoint servers are outside Tracopus; this console only manages the subscription. The working rhythm Add a subscription, send a test if offered, watch the delivery log, retry failures, disable when the partner is down for a long window. Moments that bring you here Go-live of a connector. A spike of 4xx/5xx. After rotating an endpoint URL. When automation also notifies and you must avoid double fire. ⓘ Webhooks are not the system of record A missed delivery does not mean the leave or ticket vanished. Retry the push; do not recreate the source row. Overview Webhooks fan out existing domain events. Payloads must stay masked for sensitive fields. How to use 1. HTTPS only Reject cleartext endpoints. 2. Verify signatures Integrators must check the signing secret. 3. Idempotent receivers Retries are expected. Related pages Developer portal Owning app. API keys Pull APIs vs push webhooks. pages.title: Workflow Automation
pages.description: Publish, pause, and monitor enterprise workflow rules that fire on domain events.
headings: Automation that rides on work already happening
pages.content: Workflow Automation — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin → Workflow Studio Live operations floor Automation that rides on work already happening Workflow Studio is the register of enterprise rules that listen to domain events — a leave request, an overdue approval, a ticket SLA breach, a failed integration — and then notify, route, or call a connector. It does not invent a second work tracker. Published rules fire against Employee, timesheet, leave, ticket, and approval records you already have. Drafts stay silent until you turn them on. Admin → Workflow automation Hub · Studio / Rule builder Org flag workflowsEnabled HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console See every automation in one place — published, draft, paused, failing — then publish so a rule starts matching live events, or pause so it stops without deleting the graph. KPIs cover last-week success and failure. Deep edits (trigger, conditions, actions) live on the Rule builder tab; this screen is the operations desk. Seat at the table Org administrators and HR administrators whose role can open Admin and whose org has workflow automation switched on. Contributors, managers, and finance personas do not get this menu. If the flag is off or the persona is denied, the route shows access denied — there is no employee-facing version of the studio. The working rhythm Open the studio, scan the insight strip, filter the register, then publish or pause a row. Export CSV when change-control needs a snapshot of what is live. Jump to Rule builder to change the graph, then return here to publish. Pause a live rule before you edit it so half-applied graphs never fire. Moments that bring you here After a new leave or approval policy, when you need a follow-on notify or route. When failure rate spikes and a connector is misbehaving. Before a release, to pause fragile rules. At go-live, to turn drafts on. After an incident, to export exactly what was published. Not for day-to-day task tracking — that stays on My Work and domain screens. ⓘ Rules ride on source events A published rule never becomes its own source of truth. Leave, timesheet, ticket, and approval records stay where they are; the studio only decides what happens next. Notification copy still comes from notification templates . Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Workflow studio] --> B[Filter rules] B --> C[Open a rule] C --> D[Publish or pause] D --> E[Monitor runs] E --> F[Tune in Rule builder] 1 Open studio Admin → Workflow automation. 2 Review KPIs Draft vs published vs failing. 3 Publish / pause Live events start or stop matching. 4 Tune Deep edits live on Automation rules. How to use 1. Pause before editing live rules Avoid half-applied graphs. 2. Export for review CSV is for change control, not a source of truth. 3. Builder for structure Studio is the register; Rule builder edits the graph. Related pages Automation rules Graph editor. Notification templates Messages rules may send. Audit Publish events. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Admin & Access
pages.description: Admin & Access — Tracopus user guide for enterprise work intelligence.
pages.content: Admin & Access — Tracopus User Guide Home → Admin & Access Chapter 9 · For admins & power users Admin & Access How permissions shape what you see in the Luxury UI — module menus, project scoping, timesheet date policies, and application configuration. Scenario pages document the same flags with step-by-step workflows in the Scenario User Guide . Access overview Tracopus uses role-based access control enforced on both client and server. The UI hides menus and actions you cannot use rather than showing disabled controls. Access is evaluated at multiple levels: Module level — can you see HRMS, Sales, or Project directories at all? Page level — which routes within a module appear in the sidebar? Persona level — which persona views you may switch into, and which pages each persona can open (org map + kill switches) Action level — create, edit, delete, assign, mark attendance, etc. Record level — project membership, team scope, shared vs private visibility Field level — timesheet date windows, report type availability Mobile receives an encrypted access control payload on login; web evaluates permissions from the authenticated user session. Persona access & navigation Tracopus separates who may use a persona (role) from org-wide page mapping and kill switches (organization). Surface Route Stores in What you configure Roles & permissions /admin/roles role.json → HRMS → personaModules Allowed personas, default persona, switcher; page preview writes the shared org page map. Screen guide: Roles & permissions . Simulator: Roles data flow . Persona navigation /admin/persona-navigation org.json → HRMS → personaNavigationAdditional Turn off personas/modules/pages; Page access — one page at a time, Product default vs Custom. Screen guide: Persona Navigation . Scenario: Turn off org access . Defaults Org seed: empty pagePersonaMap and empty disable lists — catalog sidebar personas[] apply until you customize a page. Site Admin role seed: all personas allowed, defaultPersona: ADMIN , switcher on. Evaluation order Role module / menu flags Role personaModules (or Automatic heuristic if never saved) Org pagePersonaMap override when present Org disabledPersonas / disabledPaths / disabledModules — always win Permission matrix on Roles stays under Advanced . Full key reference: personaNavigationAdditional and personaModules . Interactive: Roles simulator · Persona navigation simulator . Interactive data flow Trace personaModules (role layer) and personaNavigationAdditional (org layer) with live flag toggles. Role layer Roles simulator → Org layer Persona nav → All simulators Module access The left sidebar shows HRMS, Sales, and Project directories only when menuAccessControl flags them active for your user: Module Flag Typical roles HRMS hrmsModules.active All employees; HR admins see full directory Sales salesModules.active Sales, account managers, leadership Project projectModules.active Delivery, PMs, contributors Access-controlled routes These pages require additional permission flags beyond module access: File manager ( /project/filemanager ) Chat ( /project/chat ) Calendar ( /project/calendar ) Search ( /project/search ) Settings ( /hrms/settings ) Application config ( /hrms/appconfig ) Icon rail entries for these features hide when access is denied. Project access Team scope Team selection filters on list pages limit data to projects and records associated with selected teams. Your default team appears in the sidebar company chip. Project membership Project details enforce membership and team rules: Non-members may see read-only or denied views depending on shared visibility settings Cross-team access without membership renders read-only project details Members tab manages invitations, roles, and access chips Shared vs private projects Project list "Shared visibility" donut reflects how many projects are shared across teams vs restricted. Private projects appear only to members and elevated roles. Create permissions Create buttons on lists (projects, bids, POs, employees) and planner assign actions require explicit create permissions. Executive planner view is read-only when create is disabled. Timesheet access rules Timesheet permissions ( timeSheet branch of access control) govern web and mobile equally. Rule Effect enableTimeSheetEntry false No days allow entry — entire week disabled Project work item windows Billable entry only within min/max create dates derived from working-day offsets Non-project work item windows Separate date range for non-billable entries Leave/holiday rules allowLeaveAndHolidayForFuture / ForPast control leave booking direction Hour thresholds Rules like disable create before Y working days after X hours logged On mobile, disabled days show grey titles in the week list and blocked add buttons on the Record screen with snackbar message: "Time entry is not allowed for this date." Managers with multi-employee timesheet permission can switch employees on the web Timesheet page header. Work-Time Governance adds a default-off catalog (validation, approval chain, reminders, import/export, estimates, swipe evidence) configured on Admin → Feature flags . It does not replace the timesheet rules in the table above. Scenario: Enable work-time catalog features . Application configuration /hrms/appconfig — hierarchical configuration tree per team (admin access required). What admins configure Application configuration (org.json) — dropdown lists, service line trees, notification emails, feature toggles, personaNavigationAdditional Access control (role.json) — module visibility, CRUD permissions, timesheet windows, report access, personaModules Team-scoped overrides inherited from parent org nodes with lock/hide/inherit controls Role bar for assigning role templates to org units during editing Dedicated UIs: Admin → Roles (persona-first) and Admin → Persona navigation (simplified Turn off / Page access) Open full Application Configuration reference → — every key from org.json and role.json with descriptions, sample values, and UI workflow notes. Organization settings /hrms/settings — Lux settings sections: Mobile devices Register and manage employee mobile device connections. Schedulers Cron job configuration for automated tasks. Service health Monitor integrated service status. Company Organization profile and branding metadata. Localization Locale and regional preferences. Notifications Org-wide notification defaults. Personal UI preferences (palette, font) live in the Settings right sidebar and localStorage — not org-wide. Reports & feedback permissions Report types in the REPORT dropdown are filtered by permission — users only see reports they can run. Feedback template configuration and campaign launch similarly require elevated project permissions. External feedback and invoice document routes ( /document/… ) use tokenized links that bypass full app auth for respondents while keeping responses scoped. ← Back to Home © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved. Documentation Scenario Guide Getting Started Charts For support, contact your workspace administrator.

pages.title: AI Decision Audit
pages.description: Masked run metadata for AI decisions — source references, not raw prompts, and not Admin → Audit.
headings: Proof of what AI did, never the raw prompt

pages.title: Charts & Analytics
pages.description: Charts & Analytics — Tracopus user guide for enterprise work intelligence.
pages.content: Charts & Analytics — Tracopus User Guide Home → Charts & Analytics Reference Charts & Analytics Complete reference for every chart and visualization in the Luxury UI — what type it is, what data it uses, and how to interpret it for decisions. Visual types explained Web charts render via ApexCharts unless noted. Mobile Insights uses fl_chart with matching Lux card styling. Type Best for How to read Where used Donut Part-to-whole ratios Each slice = category share; center label often shows total or primary metric Status mix, billing split, portfolio outcomes Bar (H/V) Ranking categories Longer bar = higher count; horizontal for long labels Top accounts, teams, priorities, skills Area Trends over time Filled line shows volume; slope = growth/decline Creation trends, daily load, joins/exits Line Precise time series Focus on rate of change between points Headcount trend, velocity, billable trend (mobile) Funnel Stage progression Width at each stage = volume; narrowing = drop-off Bid, PO, project, taskboard pipelines Heatmap Two-dimensional intensity Darker cell = higher value Deadline heatmap, roster heatmap Radar Multi-axis comparison Shape shows strengths/weaknesses across dimensions Personal performance radar Treemap Hierarchical share Rectangle area = proportion Grade/band, portfolio effort map Bubble / Scatter Correlation + size Position = X/Y metrics; bubble size = third dimension Risk scatter, estimate vs completion Radial bar Progress toward max Arc fill = % of capacity or completion Status radial, mobile progress ring Stacked bar Composition over time Segment height = sub-category within total Hours by type, mobile daily hours Dual line Two series comparison Gap between lines = variance Planned vs logged hours (mobile) Gauge / Dual gauge Single KPI % Fill arc to target threshold Mobile utilization & billable target CSS segment bar Simple status mix Colored segments without chart library Invoice status bar Filters affect all charts: Summary charts always reflect the current list filters (teams, SHOW preset, date range, text filter). Change filters to see charts recalculate for that slice. Project list charts Full panel list on Project List guide . Quick reference: Donut panels (10): By status, Portfolio mix, Timeline health, Billing mix, PO linkage, Completed share, Open pipeline load, Automation, Shared visibility, Capex/Opex, Hours estimated Bar panels (5): Project types (H), Top accounts (H), By team (H), Priority (V), Complexity (V) Area panels (1): Creation trend (6 months) Diagrams: Delivery funnel, stage flow, estimate gaps list Accounts directory charts Panel Type Data source Data health Donut Complete records vs needs attention (missing fields) Issue breakdown H-bar distributed Counts per quality issue type Record types Donut Account vs team vs client nodes Hierarchy coverage H-bar % % accounts with teams, teams with clients, clients with email Data source Donut Salesforce-sourced vs manually created Billing type Donut Billable classification split Top by clients H-bar Largest directory nodes by client count Sales charts Bid requests: 12 chart panels + vertical funnel — see Bid Requests guide . Purchase orders: 11 chart panels + delivery funnel — see Purchase Orders guide . PO detail page adds contract-level statistics donuts/bars in the Purchase Order Detail Statistics component. HRMS & employee charts Employee directory (9 panels) Treemap, line, stacked area, 2× donut, 2× column, 2× horizontal bar — detailed in Employees guide . Personal dashboard (4 chart panels + lists) Attendance strip, 6-week stacked hours, utilization donut, task queue donut. Team manager analytics Headcount line, join/exit area, gender/location/department bars, skills distribution. Invoices (CSS visuals) Status segment bar, monthly amount bars, outstanding summary — not Apex but same summary strip location. Tasks & planner charts Task board (5 panels) Funnel diagram, workflow donut, billable scope donut, flow bar, top categories bar. Task activity register (5 panels) Status, priority, checklist, type, outcome — donuts and bars. Team capacity overview (4 panels) Utilization bar, assignment donut, daily load dual area, free capacity bar. Assign-work insight (compact) Status donut, billable/leave donut, daily area, project horizontal bars, hourly bar. Work item activity detail popover Hourly logged vs planned bar for a single activity day. Executive project dashboard charts Most diverse chart set — types include area, radar, donut, bar, radialBar, treemap, bubble, polarArea, line, heatmap. Manager delivery lens highlights Risk scatter (bubble) Bubble X/Y position maps risk dimensions; bubble size = project effort or exposure. Outliers in the "high risk" quadrant need executive attention. Deadline heatmap Heatmap Rows = teams or owners; columns = time buckets; color intensity = count of deadlines due. Dark clusters indicate scheduling crunch periods. Velocity line Line Completed deliverables or projects over time — trend line slope reflects delivery throughput. Mobile Insights charts The mobile app mirrors web analytics in four sections. Chart widgets: LuxDonutChart, LuxDualGaugeRow, LuxStackedDailyHoursChart, LuxTrendLineChart, LuxDualLineChart, LuxTrendBarChart, LuxHorizontalBarChart. LEAVE_PROMOTION_RETRY Every 15 min (optional) — retries failed TaskActivity promotion after leave approve. No. Simulators are read-only learning tools in the documentation site. They show what would happen if flags were ON or OFF — they do not call your Tracopus backend. Which simulator should I open first for leave go-live? Start with Leave policy & accrual (publish policy, import opening balances, verify accrual job), then Leave request & approve for the employee/manager workflow. Where is SQL in the simulators? Org flags come from modules.HRMS.configurations.leaveAdditional (and related paths). See Application config reference for the full key list; simulators show runtime effect per flag. © 2026 Tracopus . pages.title: External project create API
pages.description: Issue a scoped integration token, then POST /api/v2/projects with that token. Sandbox vs production only changes the key prefix — scopes are the same live catalog.
headings: Connect an external service to create projects
pages.content: External project create API — Tracopus Documentation How it works An admin issues an integration token in Tracopus (UI or admin JWT curl). The secret is shown once . The external service stores tk_live_… or tk_test_… as a secret. Do not put it in source control. The service calls POST /api/v2/projects with Authorization: Bearer {secret} . Tracopus binds the write to the key’s team. userTeamId in the body must match that team (or omit it and the server fills it). createdBy is overwritten with the key’s service employee for audit. Integration keys cannot call /api/v2/developer-portal/* . Key issue/revoke stays on an admin session. Canonical chain Projects are not independent. Create against an existing purchase order in the same team: PurchaseOrder → Project → Task → TaskActivity Minimum body for a working create: { "name": "ERP project", "userTeamId": 101, "purchaseOrderId": 9001, "createdBy": 12 } Prerequisites Item Why Server flag FS_INTEGRATION_API_KEY_AUTH_ENABLED (default true ) Maps to fs.integration.api-key-auth.enabled . If false, tk_* tokens do not authenticate (401). Admin with Integrations → API access UI path /integrations/api-access (or Admin → API keys). Developer portal + integration center must be enabled for the org. Team id, purchase order id, service employee id The PO must already exist on that team. The employee on the key is used as createdBy . Scope projects.write projects.read cannot create. Extra sandbox scopes do not exist — only the catalog below. 1 · Issue the API key Preferred: Tracopus → Integrations → API access → Create token. Choose Production ( tk_live_ ) or Sandbox ( tk_test_ ), grant projects.write , copy the secret immediately. Or create with an admin JWT (not an integration key): POST /api/v2/developer-portal/api-keys Copy curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/api/v2/developer-portal/api-keys?userTeamId=TEAM_ID" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ADMIN_JWT" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Uid: EMPLOYEE_ID" \ -H "Current-User-Team-Id: TEAM_ID" \ -d '{ "name": "ERP project sync", "appName": "External ERP", "environment": "production", "scopes": ["projects.write"], "serviceEmployeeId": EMPLOYEE_ID, "createdByEmployeeId": EMPLOYEE_ID }' Field Required Notes userTeamId query Yes Team that owns the key. Project creates must use this same team. name Yes Audit label, e.g. ERP project sync . appName No Defaults to Custom integration . environment No production → tk_live_ . sandbox → tk_test_ . Same scopes either way. scopes Yes Must include projects.write to create projects. Non-catalog values are dropped. serviceEmployeeId Yes for writes Employee stamped onto createdBy when the key creates a project. Success envelope (secret only on create): { "payload": { "key": { "id": "key-…", "prefix": "tk_live_8f2a", "scopes": ["projects.write"], "status": "active" }, "secretOnce": "tk_live_8f2a_<uuid>_<tail>" } } Store secretOnce in your secret manager. Tracopus will not show it again. Use the full string as the Bearer token — not the prefix alone. 2 · Create a project Base URL is your Tracopus API host (example: https://app.tracopus.com ). No SPA api-key query param is required for integration tokens. POST /api/v2/projects Copy curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/api/v2/projects" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer tk_live_SUFFIX_UUID_TAIL" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "name": "ERP project", "userTeamId": 101, "purchaseOrderId": 9001, "createdBy": 12, "summary": "Created from ERP sync", "status": "NEW", "type": "BILLABLE" }' Typical 200 envelope: { "payload": { "id": 44102, "name": "ERP project", "userTeamId": 101, "purchaseOrderId": 9001, "status": "NEW", "createdBy": 12 } } Project request body JSON object mapped from ProjectRequest / ProjectInfo . Dates are ISO-8601 date-times. Field Type Notes name required string Project display name. purchaseOrderId required number Existing PO on the same team. Projects hang off this contract. userTeamId required* number Must equal the key’s team. Omit to let the server inject it. Mismatch → 403. createdBy sent number Overwritten with the key’s serviceEmployeeId . summary optional string Short description. status optional string NEW , CREATED , ASSIGNED , INPROGRESS , COMPLETED , CLOSED . type / projectType optional string Delivery classification used by your org (e.g. billable vs internal). code optional string External/project code if you maintain one. owner optional number Employee id of the delivery owner. estStartTime optional datetime e.g. 2026-09-01T00:00:00 . estCompletionTime optional datetime Planned end. estHours optional number Estimated hours. currency optional string ISO currency if set on the project. location optional string Project location. clientNames optional string[] Client labels. watchers optional string[] Watcher identifiers as stored by Tracopus. accountName optional string Account label. priority / complexity optional string Org-defined values. Do not send a different userTeamId than the key’s team. Query ?userTeamId= on other endpoints is also locked to the key team. Scope catalog Production and sandbox keys share this catalog. There is no sandbox.read / sandbox.write . Scope Allows projects.read GET /api/v2/projects* projects.write POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE /api/v2/projects* — required to create purchaseorders.read GET /api/v2/purchaseorder* purchaseorders.write Write purchase orders tasks.read / tasks.write /api/v2/task* employees.read GET /api/v2/employees* integrations.read GET /api/v2/integrations/center* Auth, headers, errors Header Create key (admin) Create project (integration) Authorization Bearer admin JWT Bearer tk_live_… or tk_test_… Content-Type application/json application/json Uid Admin employee id Not required Current-User-Team-Id Admin team Not required Status Meaning 200 Created. Project is under payload . 401 / empty auth Missing Bearer, invalid secret, or API-key auth disabled on the server. 403 Missing projects.write , team mismatch, or developer-portal path called with an integration key. Body: {"error":[{"message":"Integration API key scope or team access denied"}]} or userTeamId must match integration key team . Curl builder Fill your values, generate, copy. Nothing is sent from this page. API base Integration secret Team id Purchase order id Created by (employee id) Project name Generated curl Generate Copy Tracopus integration API · project create. Token format tk_{live|test}_{suffix}_{uuid}_{tail} . Flag FS_INTEGRATION_API_KEY_AUTH_ENABLED . Open this file locally — no backend required.

pages.content: FAQ — Tracopus User Guide Home → FAQ 🔍 Jump to 📚 Documentation &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; screen guides 🎯 Scenario user guide 🔐 Login &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; account access 🧭 Navigation &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; Luxury UI 🏠 Workspace, tasks &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; approvals 👥 HRMS &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; employee records 🌴 Leave management 📍 Attendance &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; presence ⏱ Timesheet &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; time entry ✅ Timesheet approval &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; locking ⚖️ Work-Time Governance 📜 Audit trail &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; activity history 👔 People ops &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; lifecycle 📁 Projects &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; delivery 💼 Sales, bids &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; purchase orders 🧾 Invoices &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; billing 💰 Payroll &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; compensation 📈 Resource intelligence &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; staffing ⭐ Performance &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; goals 📱 Mobile app 📊 Charts &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; analytics 🔗 Integrations &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; data exchange 🛡 Admin, roles &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; security 🔧 Troubleshooting 🔑 App config · Access &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; getting started 🏢 App config · Organization tree &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; inheritance 💾 App config · Saving &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; filters 📋 App config · Application config (org.json data) 🔐 App config · Roles &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; access control ⏱ App config · Timesheet &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; work item rules 🔧 App config · Troubleshooting 282 questions · type to filter No matching questions — try different keywords. 📚 Documentation &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; screen guides 10 questions Where is the main Tracopus documentation? Open Documentation at /doucuments/index.html — screen-by-screen guides for HRMS, Project, Sales, Mobile, Charts, and Admin. What is the difference between screen docs and the Scenario Guide? Screen docs describe each UI screen (fields, charts, permissions). The Scenario Guide walks through end-to-end workflows (Feature → Scenario → Steps) for testers and end users. How do I find documentation for a specific screen? Use the header module mega-menu, home page module cards, or global search ( Ctrl + K ). Each screen doc includes breadcrumbs back to its module index. Where is Getting Started? getting-started.html — first-day orientation: login, navigation, Luxury UI, and links to HRMS, Project, and Sales modules. Where is the chart type reference? charts.html explains donut, bar, area, line, funnel, and treemap patterns used in summary strips and dashboards. How do I open Application Configuration documentation? HRMS → Application Config in docs ( hrms/application-config.html ) plus linked config FAQ sections at the bottom of this page. Are documentation pages updated with the app? Docs are static HTML in the repo — version query strings on CSS/JS ( ?v=… ) bust cache after releases. Hard-refresh if styles look stale. Can I link directly to a section in a screen doc? Yes — copy the URL with the heading anchor (e.g. hrms/timesheet.html#weekly-grid ). Breadcrumb and sidebar help you navigate back. Who maintains the documentation? Your workspace administrator or internal product team. Report gaps with the screen URL and expected behavior. Is there a printable or offline copy? Use the browser print dialog on any page. For bulk export, clone the doucuments/ folder from your deployment package. 🎯 Scenario user guide 10 questions Where is the Scenario User Guide? /documentation/user-guide/index.html — 73 scenarios across 15 modules with step-by-step instructions, including Work-Time Governance. How is a scenario page structured? Each scenario shows roles , prerequisites , numbered steps , outcome , tips, and links to related scenarios and screen docs. What extra detail do enriched scenarios include? Permissions tables, org/feature flags, warnings, role-specific behavior notes, and a QA verify checklist — useful for testers and trainers. How do I find a scenario for my task? Browse by module index, open All scenarios , or search from the scenario home. Scenarios are grouped by feature (Login, Timesheet, Bid Requests, etc.). Can I use scenarios for UAT test cases? Yes — copy the verify checklist and steps into your test plan. Link the scenario URL as traceability to requirements. Why does a scenario mention a permission I do not have? Scenarios document all supported roles. Your effective permissions come from Application Configuration role templates on your org unit. How do scenarios link to screen documentation? Related links at the bottom point to matching screen guides (e.g. timesheet scenario → hrms/timesheet.html ). How often are scenarios updated? When new modules or workflows ship. Regenerate pages with node user-guide/generate-pages.js after editing scenarios-data.js . Is the Scenario Guide different from FAQ? FAQ answers short common questions. Scenarios are procedural walkthroughs for completing real tasks end-to-end. Mobile scenarios — where are they? Scenario Guide → Mobile App module covers QR login, PIN, timesheet, tasks, and insights on Android. 🔐 Login &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; account access 10 questions How do I sign in to Tracopus? Open your organization URL, enter username and password on the Luxury login screen, then click Sign In . SSO users click Sign in with Microsoft instead. What is Microsoft SSO? Single Sign-On redirects you to Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD). After corporate authentication you return to Tracopus already logged in — no separate password required. I forgot my password — what should I do? Click Forgot Password on the login page, submit your username or email, and follow the reset link. Contact your admin if mail does not arrive within 15 minutes. Why am I stuck on the login page after SSO? Your account may be inactive, not provisioned, or missing a default team. Ask your workspace administrator to verify employee status and role assignment. How do I activate a new employee account? Open the activation link from your welcome email ( /user/activateaccount/… ), set a password, then sign in. Links expire — request a new invite from HR if needed. Can I stay signed in on my laptop? Yes — sessions persist in the browser. Always sign out on shared machines via the header account menu. Why does my session expire? Security policy may enforce idle timeout or daily re-auth. SSO tenants often require re-login after token expiry — sign in again normally. What landing page do I see after login? Your default module dashboard (Project, HRMS, or Sales) depends on role permissions configured by your administrator. How do I change my password? Account menu → Profile → Security, or use the forced change link at /user/changepassword/… when prompted. SSO user — why is password change hidden? Credentials are managed by your identity provider. Use Microsoft account settings or IT helpdesk for password resets. 🧭 Navigation &amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp;amp; Luxury UI 10 questions Where is the main module menu? The left sidebar lists HRMS, Sales, and Project modules. Expand each to see permitted screens for your role. What is the icon rail? The narrow vertical rail on the left edge provides quick links: Search, Taskboard, Calendar, Notes, Chat, Files, theme palette, and settings. How do I change the color theme? Click the palette droplet on the icon rail and pick a Luxury palette (Emerald, Indigo, Sapphire, etc.). Choice syncs to mobile after login. What does SHOW / SORT / Filter mean? Standard list header controls: SHOW = status presets, SORT = column order, Filter = text search on the register below. What is the summary strip? Collapsible KPI and chart row at the top of many list screens. Expand for analytics; collapse for a wider data table. How does global search work? Hea
