pages.title: Timesheet Approval Scenarios
pages.description: Standalone coverage map of Tracopus timesheet approval scenarios: submit, approve, reopen, resubmit, reject, and work-item promotion.
pages.content: Timesheet Approval Scenarios — Coverage Map Tracopus · HRMS · Timesheet Timesheet approval scenarios Standalone coverage map of the timesheet approval lifecycle: draft, submit, approve, reopen, resubmit, reject, unlock, auto-approve, and how hours land in work items ( TaskActivity / source=TIMESHEET ). 9 scenarios covered 9 scenarios pass 7 lifecycle steps 1 optional E2E watch Verdict: Core lifecycle is coherent end-to-end. Week status, day rows, and TIMESHEET work items stay aligned through approve → reopen → resubmit → approve/reject. Partial-week ( partialWeekSubmissionEnabled ) adds submission batches on top of the same week/day model — toggle it in the interactive data-flow simulator . Partial-week submission ( partialWeekSubmissionEnabled ) Flag Submit Pending unit Edit while pending Approve / reject Inbox id OFF (default) Full week One week row Week locked /timesheets/{weekId}/approve|reject WEEK:{id} ON Selected days ( activityDates ); multiple batches/week ts_timesheet_submission_model + day submission_id Leftover DRAFT/REJECTED days editable /timesheets/submissions/{id}/approve|reject SUBMISSION:{id} Requires timesheetApprovalEnabled . Fully APPROVED weeks still need reopen before edit. See evidence TIME-PARTIAL-WEEK-SUBMISSION.md . Happy path (status → work items) 1 Save draft Week stays DRAFT / REOPENED / REJECTED. Days → DRAFT. Work items unchanged. 2 Submit / Resubmit Week → PENDING_APPROVAL; clears prior approvedBy / rejection; REJECTED lines reactivated to ACTIVE. Work items not yet written (or remain demoted). 3 Approve Week → APPROVED. promoteWeek upserts TIMESHEET activities; leftover PENDING/DRAFT days cascade to APPROVED; orphans soft-deleted. 4 Reopen / Unlock Week → REOPENED; days → DRAFT. demoteWeek soft-deletes live TIMESHEET activities. Who: recorded approver, or manager if AUTO, or solo owner with no manager. 5 Edit + Resubmit Week → PENDING again; approval fields cleared. Work items stay demoted until next approve. 6a Approve again Revive/upsert via day.taskActivityId / natural key; soft-delete orphans. 6b Reject Week/days → REJECTED. demoteWeek ensures no live TIMESHEET hours remain. Scenarios covered S1 Draft → Submit → Approve Pass Employee saves staging, submits; manager approves. Hours become work items. Actors Employee → Manager Work items promoteWeek upsert; orphan soft-delete; leftover days cascade APPROVED Issue fixed Zero-duration days could stay PENDING after week APPROVED Fix cascadeNonRejectedDaysToApproved S2 Approve → Reopen → Edit → Resubmit → Re-approve Pass Full correction cycle after a prior promote. Actors Approver → Employee → Approver Work items demote on reopen; promote revives on re-approve Issue fixed Hours stayed live while REOPENED; orphan activities after day replace Fix demoteWeek + promote orphan cleanup S3 Approve → Reopen → Resubmit → Reject Pass Manager rejects after a prior promotion existed. Actors Approver → Employee → Approver Work items demoteWeek on reject — no live TIMESHEET rows Issue fixed Reject left APPROVED TaskActivities; utilization still showed hours Fix demoteWeek in processReject S4 Line reject → fix → Resubmit → Approve Pass Single line rejected, employee corrects, week resubmitted and approved. Actors Manager → Employee → Manager Work items Line reactivated ACTIVE; promote includes hours again Issue fixed lineStatus stuck REJECTED; promoteWeek skipped the line Fix reactivateRejectedLines + staging save reactivation S5 Dirty Save + Submit (first week) Pass Employee edits cells and clicks Submit while unsaved. Actors Employee Work items N/A until approve Issue fixed Save callback dropped payload; setState race missed weekId Fix Forward save payload into submit (TimesheetPage + Employee360) S6 Auto-approve-own then reopen Pass Submit with auto-approve → APPROVED ( approvalAuthorityType=AUTO ). Actors Employee (submit); Manager or solo owner (reopen) Work items Promoted on auto-approve path Issue fixed Employee always saw Reopen; solo owner with no manager was stuck Fix Has manager → only canAct reopens. No manager → owner may self-reopen S7 ADD TIME ENTRY by status Pass Header / board create CTA gated by week status. Allowed DRAFT, REJECTED, REOPENED Blocked PENDING, APPROVED, LOCKED Issue fixed ADD ENTRY clickable on APPROVED Fix canAddTimesheetEntry S8 Unlock locked week Pass LOCKED → unlock → REOPENED; days DRAFT; work items demoted. Actors Manager / delegate Work items demoteWeek on unlock Issue fixed Unlock left promoted hours live Fix demoteWeek in unlockWeeks S9 Orphan day replace after edit Pass Approve₁ → reopen → change hours on same date → re-approve (canonical day kept). Actors Employee → Approver Work items Old TIMESHEET activity soft-deleted; current reused/updated Issue fixed Extra work-item hours (e.g. 11h vs 9h) from superseded day Fix Canonical days by line+date + orphan activity soft-delete UI gates by status Status Employee Manager DRAFT ADD ENTRY · Save · Submit — PENDING Locked · no ADD · Remind Approve / Reject (not own week) APPROVED No ADD · Reopen only if AUTO + no manager Reopen if approvedBy, or canAct if AUTO REOPENED ADD · Edit · Resubmit View REJECTED ADD · Resubmit — LOCKED No ADD · blocked Unlock → REOPENED + demote Work-item reflection On approve — promote TimesheetPromotionService.promoteWeek writes TaskActivity with source=TIMESHEET , links day/week ids, approvalStatus=APPROVED . Soft-deletes orphans not kept. After demote, revive uses day.taskActivityId . On reject / reopen / unlock — demote demoteWeek soft-deletes live TIMESHEET activities for the week. Non-TIMESHEET sources (TASK_BOARD / LEGACY) are left alone. Day links kept for revive. Residual / watch Area Note Risk Solo auto-approve owner No reporting manager + AUTO: employee may self-reopen. With a manager, only manager/delegate canAct. Fixed Legacy weeks (null approvedBy) Reopen falls back to canAct (manager/delegate), not employee. By design Live staging / Playwright Unit/FE tests cover paths; full browser assert of work items after S2/S3 optional. pages.title: Timesheet Approval
pages.description: Submit weeks or day batches for manager approval, resolve conflicts, and lock payroll periods.
headings: Submit, conflict, lock — the manager pass
pages.content: Timesheet Approval — Tracopus User Guide Home → HRMS → Timesheet Approval Week decisions Submit, conflict, lock — the manager pass Timesheet approval is the manager pass: submitted weeks (or day batches), conflict resolution, and payroll-period lock. It sits on the same timesheet records the grid wrote. People → Timesheets (approval) Route /people/timesheet Manager · HR Admin · Payroll (lock window) The job of this console Approve or reject a week, resolve overlapping hours, and understand when lock freezes the period. Do not re-key hours here unless the product offers a correction path. Seat at the table Managers of people who submit. Employees submit from the grid. Payroll cares about lock, not individual cells. The working rhythm Open the approval queue, filter the week, open conflicts, approve or reject, then lock when the org’s payroll calendar says so. Moments that bring you here Monday after submit. Two projects claiming the same afternoon. Payroll cutoff. A missing leave row that should have filled hours. ⓘ Same timesheet, second seat This is not a second timesheet table. Lock is part of the protected timesheet flow. Interactive data flow Same timesheet simulator — toggle partialWeekSubmissionEnabled for full-week vs day-batch pending, manager/delegate approve, and lock/reopen paths. Primary simulator Timesheet flags & approval → Delegation & inbox Flowcharts Each diagram auto-plays steps when it scrolls into view. Use Play / Pause , or click a step to jump. flowchart TD O[Open week] --> Sub[Submit] Sub --> Pend[Pending manager] Pend --> Dec{Decision} Dec -->|Approve| Apr[Approved] Dec -->|Reject| Rej[Reject + comment] Rej --> Fix[Employee fixes] Fix --> Sub Apr --> Lock[Payroll lock] 1 Open week Hours entered on Timesheet. 2 Submit Employee submits for approval. 3 Pending manager Appears in pending panel / Approvals. 4 Decision Approve or reject with comment. 5 Approved Week accepted for payroll. 6 Reject + comment Employee notified to fix. 7 Employee fixes Edit open week and resubmit. 8 Payroll lock Manager/HR locks; corrections need unlock. flowchart TD Pend[Pending week] --> Conf{Conflicts?} Conf -->|Yes| Modal[Conflict modal] Modal --> Resolve[Resolve / edit] Resolve --> Pend Conf -->|No| Approve[Approve] 1 Pending week Manager opens approval item. 2 Conflicts? Overlaps or policy violations. 3 Conflict modal Shows conflicting rows. 4 Resolve / edit Fix hours or send back. 5 Approve Proceed when clean. Overview Timesheet approval adds submit, manager review, conflict resolution, and payroll lock on top of the weekly grid. Delegation may allow acting approvers. When Work-Time late-workflow is on, late weeks can require a late reason on submit and may route through published late bands ( TIMESHEET-LATE-LTE7 / TIMESHEET-LATE-GT7 ) instead of the standard chain. Partial-week flag ( timesheetAdditional.partialWeekSubmissionEnabled , default off): Off — employee submits the full week; one pending week; week locked until approve/reject; inbox id WEEK:{id} . On — employee selects days (chips) and may submit multiple batches per week; each batch is a separate approval request ( ts_timesheet_submission_model ); leftover DRAFT/REJECTED days stay editable; approve/reject by submission; inbox id SUBMISSION:{id} . Fully APPROVED weeks still require reopen before edit. How to use 1. Employee submits Full week when partial is off; select day chips and submit a batch when partial is on. If Work-Time late-workflow is on and the week is past cut-off, the employee must complete a late reason first. 2. Manager reviews Pending panel or Approvals inbox (week or submission card). Late weeks may arrive on the moderately late chain ( TIMESHEET-LATE-LTE7 , business-unit) or the significantly late chain ( TIMESHEET-LATE-GT7 , business-unit then finance) when those policies are published. 3. Resolve conflicts Clear overlaps before approve (scoped to the pending week or batch). Late reason is audit context — the employee does not pick the approval route. 4. Approve or reject Approve to complete the step, or reject with a comment so the employee can fix and resubmit. 5. Lock when ready Payroll / role month lock still applies. With timesheet.period-lock on and lockAfterDays set (often 7), approved weeks also auto-lock via TIMESHEET_PERIOD_LOCK ; reopen may require a reason. Related pages Timesheet Weekly entry grid. Work-Time Governance Approval chain, bulk actions, legacy fallback. Audit Trail Week-level events. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Timesheet
pages.description: Monday–Sunday grid for billable, non-billable, and leave hours — with week navigation, validation, and optional approval.
headings: Hours on work already in the system
pages.content: Timesheet — Tracopus User Guide Home → HRMS → Timesheet Monday–Sunday grid Hours on work already in the system Timesheet is the Monday–Sunday grid for billable, non-billable, and leave hours — week navigation, validation, and optional approval. Rows point at projects and tasks you already have. People → Timesheets Route /hrms/timesheet Employee · Manager (approval) The job of this console Log the week, pass validation, submit if the org requires approval, and stop editing when the period locks. Leave hours should follow approved leave, not a parallel guess. Seat at the table Employees fill their grid. Managers approve. Finance and payroll consume after lock. Project managers do not treat this as a task tracker. The working rhythm Pick the week, enter hours against work items, validate, submit, then wait for approval if enabled. Fix rejects on the same week. Do not invent a project code that does not exist. Moments that bring you here Friday fill. A week with leave in the middle. Validation blocking overtime. Before payroll lock. After a project code change. ⓘ Protected production flow Entry, approval, and locking stay on the live timesheet engine. Intelligence hooks may advise; they do not replace the grid as source. Interactive data flow Toggle timesheet approval flags — full-week vs partial-week ( partialWeekSubmissionEnabled ), submit, manager approve, reopen, and TaskActivity promotion. Primary simulator Timesheet flags & approval → All simulators Flowcharts Each diagram auto-plays steps when it scrolls into view. Use Play / Pause , or click a step to jump. flowchart TD W[Select week] --> E[Add / edit entries] E --> V[Validation summary] V --> S{Approval on?} S -->|No| Done[Week saved] S -->|Yes| Sub[Submit for approval] 1 Select week Header arrows move Monday–Sunday weeks. 2 Add / edit entries Billable, non-billable, or leave hours. 3 Validation summary Totals, billable ratio, policy hints. 4 Approval on? Org timesheet approval workflow. 5 Week saved Open weeks editable until lock. 6 Submit for approval Manager queue — see Timesheet Approval guide. flowchart TD Add[Add entry] --> Type{Type} Type -->|Billable| Proj[Pick project / deliverable] Type -->|Non-billable| NB[Internal code] Type -->|Leave| Lv[Leave / holiday] Proj --> Hrs[Enter hours] NB --> Hrs Lv --> Hrs Hrs --> Save[Save cell] 1 Add entry Header Add entry or day cell click. 2 Type Billable, non-billable, or leave. 3 Pick project / deliverable Required for billable client work. 4 Internal code Training, admin, etc. 5 Leave / holiday May sync from approved leave. 6 Enter hours H or H.MM per org config. 7 Save cell Row refreshes totals. Overview HRMS → Time Sheet is the weekly hour grid. When timesheet approval is enabled, submit and manager review apply — see the Approval guide. With partialWeekSubmissionEnabled on, you can submit selected days as separate batches while leftover draft days stay editable; with the flag off (default), submit covers the whole week. Sync external leaves when integrations allow. When Work-Time Governance catalog features are effective, a governance banner can appear for validation, late bands, or lock policy. With timesheet.reminders or timesheet.late-workflow on, the page loads a server deadline preview for the selected week (it does not guess Friday 18:00 locally). When late-workflow requires a reason, Submit shows a late-reason field. Submit still uses this grid — governance does not add a second timesheet. How to use 1. Open the current week Confirm week range in the header. Changing week or team refreshes the deadline preview. 2. Log hours daily Prefer daily entry over Friday catch-up. 3. Link billable work Select the correct project/deliverable. 4. Check deadline / late reason If the week is past the configured cut-off and late-workflow is on, complete the late-reason field before Submit (Other needs detail). 5. Submit if required Full week when partial is off; use day chips to submit batches when partial is on. See Timesheet Approval. Related pages Timesheet Approval Submit, approve, lock. Work-Time Governance Validation catalog, chain, import/export. Leave Management Leave rows on the grid. Employee Dashboard Utilization charts. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Work-Time Governance
pages.description: Default-off catalog for timesheet validation, approval chains, reminders, import/export, estimates, and attendance evidence — configured from Feature Flags.
headings: Families that stay off until you switch them on
Deadline preview, late reason, reminders, and lock
pages.content: Work-Time Governance — Tracopus User Guide Home → HRMS → Work-Time Governance Code-owned catalog Families that stay off until you switch them on Work-Time Governance is a code-owned catalog of timesheet, approval, planning, attendance, and integration features. Catalog defaults are off. Application Config and the Feature flags console are how families go live. Admin → Feature flags (Work-Time Governance panel) HR Admin · Org Admin The job of this console Understand which family you are about to enable, the dependents, and the screens that will appear. Enable from Feature flags / Application Config — this page is the map, not a second toggle UI. Seat at the table Administrators designing time rules. Employees never enable catalog families. The working rhythm Read the family, check dependents, enable on Feature flags, then prove timesheet, attendance, or approval still behave. Roll back the flag if a family is not ready. Moments that bring you here Before turning on approval chain. A planning feature that surprised managers. After an upgrade that added catalog entries. When two families overlap. ⓘ Defaults are off Shipping code is not the same as enabling a family. Application Config still holds related keys; this catalog does not store hours. Interactive data flow Work-Time Governance sits on top of the existing timesheet approval flags. Use the timesheet simulator for submit/approve/lock, then return here for catalog families and resolver rules. Primary simulator Timesheet flags & approval → Config Application Config → Admin scenario Flowcharts Each diagram auto-plays steps when it scrolls into view. Use Play / Pause , or click a step to jump. flowchart TD Cat[Catalog default off] --> App[Application Config] App --> Proj{Project override?} Proj -->|No| Role Proj -->|Yes| Role[Role gate AND] Role --> Dep[Dependencies AND] Dep --> Eff[Effective enabled] 1 Catalog default Code owns identity, family, and default-off. 2 Application Config Tenant / org unit choice stored on the HRMS module. 3 Project override? Optional per-project on/off when the feature allows project scope. 4 Role gate AND Bulk actions, import/export, and admin policy require matching role flags. 5 Dependencies AND Escalation needs chain; FTE needs estimates; WFH needs source resolution. 6 Effective enabled Feature Flags panel shows Enabled, Blocked, or Off. flowchart TD Day[Work day] --> Leave{Approved leave?} Leave -->|Yes| Out[Leave evidence] Leave -->|No| Swipe{Swipe ingest on?} Swipe -->|Hit| Out2[Swipe evidence] Swipe -->|Miss| Wfh{Timesheet WFH on?} Wfh -->|Hours| Out3[WFH from timesheet] Wfh -->|No| Reg{Regularization?} Reg -->|Yes| Out4[Override] Reg -->|No| Empty[No composed source] 1 Work day Resolve one employee-day at a time. 2 Approved leave? Leave remains first and is not replaced by hours. 3 Swipe ingest Raw swipe rows persist only when attendance.swipe-ingest is on. 4 Timesheet WFH Approved timesheet hours can mark WFH when that feature is on. 5 Regularization Existing attendance regularization can override the composed view. 6 Composed source Read API only — the Attendance matrix stays the write store. Overview Work-Time Governance is not a second timesheet product. It is a switchboard: about twenty catalog features grouped into approval, timesheet, planning, attendance, integration, and admin families. Turning a feature on does not invent a new source table. Hours still live on timesheet activity, projects still live on Purchase Order → Project → Task → Task Activity, and attendance marks still live on the attendance matrix. The Feature Flags panel shows each feature’s inherited value, optional project override, role gate, and whether a missing dependency is blocking it. Effective state is Enabled , Blocked (selected on but role or dependency failed), or Off . How to configure 1. Open Feature Flags Requires adminGovernanceEnabled and featureFlagsAdminEnabled . Scroll to the Work-Time Governance panel. 2. Enable a family, then dependents Example: enable approval.chain before escalation or bulk actions. Enable planning.estimates before FTE or variance. 3. Save Application Config Tenant choices persist on the HRMS module. Pilot on a child org unit before root lock. 4. Optional project override Enter a project id on the panel to overlay on/off for features that allow project scope. Delete the override to inherit the team value again. 5. Confirm on Timesheet When timesheet.reminders or timesheet.late-workflow is on, the page loads a server deadline preview for the selected week. Late weeks can show a late-reason field on Submit. Submit still uses the protected timesheet workflow. Catalog families Catalog keys are stable ids. Defaults in code are off; organisation seeds may turn selected features on for a tenant. Family Feature ids What it does Approval approval.chain , approval.escalation , approval.bulk-actions Versioned policy/steps, escalation, and role-gated bulk actions. Timesheet can keep legacy manager approval when approvalChainFallbackLegacy is true. Timesheet timesheet.validation , approval-units , reminders , late-workflow , period-lock , variance , allocation WARN/BLOCK validation, weekly approval units, deadline preview and reminder offsets, late bands with required reason, period lock after lockAfterDays , and planning bridges. Does not replace the existing timesheet grid. Planning planning.estimates , planning.fte , planning.variance Grade / skill / resource estimate dimensions and optional FTE gate. Variance is a report over Task Activity hours. Attendance attendance.swipe-ingest , source-resolution , timesheet-wfh , cross-midnight , period-lock Connector-gated swipe rows and a composed read of leave → swipe → WFH hours → regularization. attendance.period-lock has no lock service yet — do not treat it as active. Integration integration.project-import , integration.timesheet-export Vendor-neutral adapters with mapping, least-privilege scopes, and idempotency. A vendor-specific adapter is not bundled. Admin admin.policy-management , admin.observability Role-gated policy editors and observability inventory for operators. Deadline preview, late reason, reminders, and lock Deadline preview — when timesheet.reminders or timesheet.late-workflow is on (and approval.chain is effective), the timesheet page calls GET …/timesheets/deadline-preview for the selected week. The UI follows that preview; it does not guess Friday 18:00 locally. If both features are off, preview is DISABLED and not late. Late reason — when timesheet.late-workflow is on and the preview reports reasonRequired , Submit shows a late-reason field (Other needs detail). Exactly seven elapsed days follows the moderately late band ( TIMESHEET-LATE-LTE7 ); later follows TIMESHEET-LATE-GT7 . Changing week or team clears leftover submit governance so an on-time week does not keep a prior late reason. Validation — timesheet.validation can WARN (submit allowed with hints) or BLOCK. Reminders — catalog timesheet.reminders supplies cut-off day and offsets (default Friday 18:00 UTC, 3 / 1 / 0). Emails still need the master flag timesheetAdditional.timesheetSubmissionReminderEnabled and the reminder job. Master off blocks emails even if the catalog reminder is on. Period lock — with timesheet.period-lock on, lockAfterDays greater than 0 (tenant seed often 7 ), and job TIMESHEET_PERIOD_LOCK , approved weeks lock. Reopen can require a reason. The older month lock disableLastMonthAfterXDays still applies separately. Approval units — weekly units can feed the chain engine. If no TIMESHEET chain policy is published, approvalChainFallbackLegacy=true keeps the existing manager approval path. Approval chain and inbox When approval.chain is effective and a domain policy is published, instances appear with step metadata. My Approvals remains the action inbox; it does not store a second copy of the timesheet. Escalation and bulk actions require the chain feature plus their own flags (bulk is role-gated). Delegation still

pages.content: API Access — Tracopus User Guide Home → Integrations → API access Inbound tokens How an external system is allowed in API access issues scoped tokens for callers of Tracopus APIs. It is not the Admin key vault and not a Salesforce password. Integrations → API access Route /integrations/api-access Org flag apiAccessEnabled Integration admin · Admin The job of this console Issue least privilege, give it to the caller, rotate, revoke when the project ends. Prove calls on the Integration API console. Seat at the table Integration admins and admins with apiAccessEnabled. Tokens inherit RBAC — they are not god keys. The working rhythm Create, prove, hand off, rotate, revoke. Moments that bring you here A new middleware. External project create. Replacing a shared user login. pages.title: Luxury Interface
pages.description: Luxury Interface — Tracopus user guide for enterprise work intelligence.
pages.content: Luxury Interface — Tracopus User Guide Home → Luxury Interface Chapter 2 Luxury Interface How to navigate the updated shell — glass surfaces, collapsible analytics, icon rail shortcuts, and personalization that carries across web and mobile. Shell layout The Luxury UI uses a three-column mental model on desktop: Icon rail (narrow, leftmost) — persistent quick actions and personalization. Module sidebar — directory navigation for HRMS, Sales, or Project pages you have access to. Main canvas — page header, optional summary analytics strip, filters, and content (table, grid, kanban, or dashboard). On mobile, the module sidebar collapses; the header exposes grid/list/create shortcuts where applicable. Page header Every main page shows: Workspace kicker — HRMS, Sales, or Project label above the page title. Page title — e.g. "Project List", "Time Sheet", "Bid Requests". Global search field — type and press Enter to open /project/search with results across entities. Dropdown panels — Tasks, Chat, Notifications (quick previews with links to full pages). Account menu — Profile, Settings, Sign out (or Microsoft logout when using SSO). Tip: Use header search for fast jumps to projects, tasks, or people instead of drilling through menus. Module sidebar Under Directories , expand HRMS, Sales, or Project to see permitted menu items. Items you cannot access are hidden entirely — not grayed out. The company chip below the logo shows your default team name, helping you confirm organizational context. Typical Project menu items Dashboard, Project List, Team capacity, Accounts, Notes, Taskboard, Task Activity, Reports, Feedback. Typical HRMS menu items Dashboard, Employees, Attendance, Time Sheet, Invoice. Typical Sales menu items Bid Requests, Purchase Orders. Icon rail The narrow rail on the far left provides cross-module shortcuts: Icon Action Search Opens global search page Taskboard Jump to kanban view Calendar Personal work calendar (access-controlled) Notes Quick notes overlay / Notes page Chat Messaging (access-controlled) Files File manager (access-controlled) Palette droplet Color theme picker App config Application configuration tree (admin) Settings Right sidebar with layout & font options Today Today activity sidebar Avatar User menu duplicate of header account Global search Type your query in the header search field. Press Enter to navigate to the search results page. Results are grouped by entity type; click a row to open the detail view. Search respects your access permissions — you only see records your role allows. Themes & color palettes Twelve curated palettes change primary, accent, and soft background tokens across the entire app. Emerald is the default theme for this documentation site. Your choice is saved in browser storage ( docs-lux-palette for this guide; the live app stores your palette preference separately and syncs to mobile). Preview palettes Click a swatch to preview — saved locally in this documentation site and synced with the live app key. Available palettes Indigo (default), Sapphire, Emerald, Rose, Midnight, Amber, Violet, Ocean, Sunset, Graphite, Crimson, Forest. Midnight and Graphite apply a darker shell treatment. Change palette via: icon rail droplet, Settings right sidebar link, or the preview grid above (syncs with the live app). Typography & layout settings Open Settings from the icon rail to adjust: Font family — Inter (default), Source Sans 3, IBM Plex Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans, DM Sans, Roboto, Open Sans, Lato, Manrope, Montserrat, and more. Layout toggles — compact sidebar and related display preferences. Font choice is stored in the app UI settings (browser local storage) and applied via data-lux-font on the document root. Summary panels List and dashboard pages open with a collapsible Lux summary section containing: KPI strip (counts, totals, percentages) Highlight / insight cards with stacked bar segments Stage flow or funnel diagrams (horizontal pipelines) Chart gallery (donut, bar, area, line panels — see Charts reference ) Collapse state is remembered per page in localStorage so your preference persists between visits. List page controls Most register pages (projects, employees, bids, etc.) share a filter bar: Team selection — multi-select checkbox menu to scope data Filter list… — free-text search within the current result set SHOW — status preset (Active, Archived, My projects, etc.) SORT — field and direction Date range — where applicable (projects, reports) Quick filter chips — one-click presets below the summary Grid / List toggle — switch table vs card grid Create — opens sidebar wizard or form (permission-gated) Create wizards vs forms Major create flows offer Wizard and Form modes via a toggle at the top of the sidebar: Project — 6+ steps: setup, client & study, service scope, fieldwork, compliance, team & estimates Purchase order — contract core, client, delivery scope, references Bid request — study basics, setup, screening, additional, quota Employee — profile, access, sign-in, organization, skills Use Wizard for guided first-time creation; switch to Form for quick edits by experts. Next: Projects → © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved. Documentation Scenario Guide Getting Started Charts For support, contact your workspace administrator.

pages.content: Requisitions — Tracopus User Guide Home → People → Requisitions Open roles Demand the pipeline hangs from Requisitions are the ATS openings. Candidates, interviews, and offers point here. Project staffing requests are a different demand stream. People → Requisitions Route /recruiting/requisitions Org flag recruitingEnabled HR Admin · Admin The job of this console Open a role, keep it accurate, attach pipeline, close when filled. Do not use this list as the org chart. Seat at the table HR Admin and Admin. Hiring managers may collaborate on their reqs if the product scopes them. The working rhythm Create or filter, edit the opening, watch attached candidates, close on hire or cancel. Moments that bring you here New approved headcount. A backfill. Freeze. After an offer is signed. ⓘ Not a project and not Employee Filled work still needs an Employee row before timesheet and leave. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Requisitions] --> B[Create or edit req] B --> C[Pipeline candidates] C --> D[Interviews / offer] D --> E[Fill or cancel] E --> F[Employee + onboarding if hired] 1 Open People → Requisitions. 2 Author Role and hiring manager. 3 Pipeline Candidates hang off the req. 4 Close Hired becomes Employee. Overview Requisitions are ATS demand. Resources staffing requests are project load. Do not treat a req as a Project. How to use 1. One req per role opening Not per applicant. 2. Fill path Offer → Employee → onboarding. 3. Cancel cleanly Do not leave ghost openings for capacity. Related pages Recruiting Funnel. Candidates People in pipeline. Staffing requests Project demand. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.content: Bench & Roll-off — Tracopus User Guide Home → Resources → Bench & roll-off Ready pool Who is free next — from real assignments ending Bench & roll-off shows Employee availability as projects end. It is supply for staffing, not a performance ranking. Resources → Bench & roll-off Route /resources/bench Org flag benchEnabled Resource Manager · Project Manager The job of this console See who is coming free, match to a request, place on Team capacity, watch the bench row clear. Seat at the table Resource and project managers. Employees may see their own end date on My work, not this board as authors. The working rhythm Scan roll-offs, open a request, place, confirm utilization. Moments that bring you here End of a PO. A gap next month. After a cancellation. Staffing standup. ⓘ Derived from assignments Not candidates. Not a second Employee list. Performance is a different module. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Bench] --> B[See available / roll-off] B --> C[Staffing request or capacity] C --> D[Assign Employee] D --> E[Bench row clears] 1 Open Resources → Bench & roll-off. 2 Supply Employee availability. 3 Place Request or capacity. 4 Clear They are allocated. Overview Bench is availability derived from assignments ending. Performance reviews are a different module. Candidates are ATS. How to use 1. Treat as supply Not a shame board. 2. Roll-off dates Come from project assignments. 3. Upskill Learning assignments while waiting. Related pages Staffing requests Demand. Team capacity Place. Performance reviews Different. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Capacity Simulation
pages.description: What-if staffing and bench moves before you commit the roster — Team capacity remains the live planner.
headings: Try the move before the roster is true
pages.content: Capacity Simulation — Tracopus User Guide Home → Resources → Capacity simulation Sandbox Try the move before the roster is true Capacity simulation models staffing and bench moves without writing the live roster. Commit stays on Team capacity. Resources → Capacity simulation Route /resources/planner Org flag plannerEnabled Resource Manager · Project Manager The job of this console Build a scenario, test a move, compare, then apply on the live planner if leadership agrees. Seat at the table Resource and project managers. Employees do not sandbox their own week here. The working rhythm Open sim, change, compare, commit elsewhere or discard. Moments that bring you here Before a big start date. Bench overflow. A what-if for a bid. After a resignation. ⓘ Not live assignments Timesheet and delivery read Team capacity / assignments, not this sandbox. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Capacity simulation] --> B[Build scenario] B --> C[Move people / demand] C --> D[Compare to live] D --> E{Commit?} E -->|Yes| F[Team capacity] E -->|No| G[Discard / save sandbox] 1 Open Resources → Capacity simulation. 2 Model Sandbox moves. 3 Compare Live Team capacity. 4 Commit Only on the live planner. Overview Simulation is a sandbox. Team capacity writes live assignments on Employee and Project. Utilization is the demand/load lens. How to use 1. Do not treat sandbox as roster Finance and timesheet read live assignments. 2. Name scenarios Or you will apply the wrong one. 3. Staffing requests Fulfill from live capacity, not only the sim. Related pages Team capacity Live planner. Utilization & demand Load lens. Staffing requests Demand tickets. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.content: Purchase Orders — Tracopus User Guide Home → Sales → Purchase Orders Contracts The purchase order that may spawn delivery Purchase orders is the contract list — POs that may link to bids and spawn delivery projects. In Tracopus, purchase contract means this PurchaseOrder register. Finance → Purchase orders Route /finance/purchaseorders Finance Manager · Admin The job of this console Find a contract, open details, understand links to bids and projects. Create POs through the allowed intake (including imports), not by opening a project first. Seat at the table Finance administrators. PMs consume the project after spawn. Employees do not maintain POs. The working rhythm Filter the list, open a PO, confirm bid and project links, only then expect delivery screens to light up. Moments that bring you here Won bid conversion. Salesforce import. A project with a missing parent PO. Revenue questions that should start here, not on a dashboard. ⓘ PurchaseOrder is canonical Do not create a shadow contract list. Projects hang off this entity when the chain is used. headings: How to do it — step by step
pages.content: Home — Tracopus Scenario Guide Home Tracopus · Scenario User Guide How to do it — step by step Every workflow documented as Feature → Scenario → Steps . Use this guide for onboarding, QA test scripts, and day-to-day help when you need to complete a task in Tracopus. ℹ️ How this guide is organized Pick a module below, then a feature , then open the scenario you need. Each scenario includes permissions , org/feature flags , warnings , role-specific behavior notes , numbered steps, verification checklist, and links to screen reference docs. ⚠️ Before you test Confirm Application Config flags and role permissions for your pilot org unit. Behavior changes when flags are off — menus hide rather than show disabled controls. Use persona-specific test accounts (employee, manager, HR admin). Feature (e.g. Employees) → Scenario (e.g. Create a new employee) → Steps (numbered actions) Screen documentation This guide covers how to complete workflows . For page-by-page screen reference — charts, filters, permissions tables, and FAQs — use the main documentation. pages.title: My Approvals
pages.description: Universal approval inbox — filter by status, domain, and priority, then approve or reject without leaving the page.
headings: One queue for leave, time, attendance, and more
pages.content: My Approvals — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → My Approvals Universal inbox One queue for leave, time, attendance, and more My Approvals is the universal inbox — filter by status, domain, and priority, then approve or reject without leaving the page. Items are the same requests the domain screens created. Workspace → My approvals Route /workspace/approvals Org flag approvalsEnabled Employee (own) · Manager · HR · Payroll · Finance · Executive · Admin The job of this console Clear the queue: filter, open enough context, approve or reject. Delegation may put someone else’s items here. Do not approve by editing the source timesheet unless you are correcting, not deciding. Seat at the table Anyone who receives work from published approval policies. Administrators still author policies under Admin. The working rhythm Open My approvals, filter domain, act in bulk or one-by-one, confirm the domain screen shows the new status. Use comments when rejecting. Moments that bring you here Monday manager pass. Payroll week. After a delegate starts. A SLA that is about to breach. When someone asks ‘where did my leave go’ — it is here or on Leave management. ⓘ Inbox, not a new request type Leave, timesheet, attendance, and access requests stay on their source tables. Policies and ApprovalAuthority still decide who sees a row. Interactive data flow Universal inbox merges leave, timesheet, and attendance pending rows — delegation scopes control who can act. Primary simulator Approval delegation & inbox → All simulators Flowcharts Each diagram auto-plays when it scrolls into view. Use Play / Pause , or click a step to jump. flowchart TD A[Open My Approvals] --> B[Filter pending] B --> C[Open request] C --> D{Approve or Reject} D -->|Approve| E[Optional comment] D -->|Reject| F[Comment required] E --> G[Inbox refreshes] F --> G 1 Open My Approvals Workspace → My approvals (or header shortcut when enabled). 2 Filter pending Status defaults to Pending. Narrow by domain, priority, or search. 3 Open request Click a register row to open the detail drawer. 4 Approve or Reject Approve may allow an optional comment; reject usually requires one. 5 Inbox refreshes List and KPIs update after the action succeeds. flowchart TD S[SLA banner] --> H[Review high priority] H --> I[Pending + High filter] I --> R[Clear overdue first] A2[Analytics tab] --> D2[Domain bottlenecks] 1 SLA banner Appears when items are overdue or due within 48 hours. 2 Review high priority Banner CTA focuses Pending + High priority. 3 Analytics tab Hero nav switches to queue health by domain and aging. Overview My Approvals aggregates decisions you (or you as delegate) can take across HRMS and delivery domains. Source records stay in their modules; this page is the action inbox, not a second data store. When Work-Time Governance approval.chain is effective and a policy is published, chain step metadata can appear on items. Until then, timesheet rows keep the existing manager path when approvalChainFallbackLegacy is true. See Work-Time Governance . How to use 1. Start on Pending Status chips default to Pending. Use All only when auditing history. 2. Narrow the queue Domain and Priority dropdowns, plus search on requester/subject/module. 3. Act from the drawer Open a row, review context, approve or reject, then refresh if needed. 4. Save a view Use saved views for recurring filters (e.g. Leave + High). Related pages Timesheet Approval Domain-specific timesheet decisions. Work-Time Governance Catalog chain, escalation, bulk actions. Leave Management Leave requests that feed the inbox. Notification templates Emails and in-app copy for approval events. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Workspace Home
pages.description: Persona-aware home with shortcuts to approvals, work, and notifications — a launch pad, not a second work tracker.
headings: Shortcuts to work you already own
pages.content: Workspace Home — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → Home Launch pad Shortcuts to work you already own Home greets you with persona-aware doors into My work, approvals, and notifications. It does not keep a second list of tasks, pay, or tickets. Workspace → Home Route /workspace/home Org flag homeEnabled All signed-in personas The job of this console Orient for the day, then jump. Read what is waiting, open the owning screen, and leave Home behind until the next landing. Seat at the table Every signed-in person with homeEnabled. Cards you cannot open stay hidden by persona navigation and flags — not by deleting the route. The working rhythm Land, scan shortcuts, click one destination, act there. Return only when you need a different door. Moments that bring you here First screen after login. After a role switch. When you cannot remember whether something lives under People or Projects. ⓘ Home is not a source Tasks stay on Task / TaskActivity. Approvals stay on domain requests. Paychecks stay on payroll publishes. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Workspace Home] --> B[Read persona shortcuts] B --> C{Need to act?} C -->|Assigned work| D[My work] C -->|Decisions| E[My approvals] C -->|Alerts| F[Notifications] D --> G[Update Task or TaskActivity] E --> H[Decide on source request] F --> I[Open the linked record] 1 Open Home Workspace → Home after sign-in. 2 Read the strip Shortcuts match your persona and flags. 3 Jump Open My work, Approvals, or Notifications. 4 Act there Home never stores the work item. Overview Workspace Home is a persona-aware launch pad over Employee, Task, TaskActivity, and approval inboxes you already have. Cards are shortcuts, not a shadow backlog. How to use 1. Treat cards as doors Click through; do not expect to complete a timesheet on Home. 2. Persona changes the map A manager sees approvals; an employee may not. 3. Favorites are personal They do not change org navigation policy. Related pages My work Assigned tasks and activities. My approvals Universal inbox. Notifications Alerts that deep-link to records. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: My Onboarding
pages.description: Tasks on your live onboarding case — documents, acknowledgements, and HR checkpoints — not a second HR file.
headings: Your case, not a second employee record
pages.content: My Onboarding — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → My onboarding Joiner checklist Your case, not a second employee record My onboarding lists tasks on the case HR opened for you. Completing a row updates that case; it does not create a new Employee. Workspace → My onboarding Route /people/onboarding/my-tasks Org flag onboardingSelfServiceEnabled Employee (new joiner) The job of this console Work through assigned tasks — documents, acknowledgements, forms — until the case is clear. Escalate to HR when a task is blocked on them. Seat at the table New joiners with onboardingSelfServiceEnabled. HR uses People → Onboarding. Managers may see status, not this checklist as authors. The working rhythm Open daily until done, complete what you can, stop when the remaining items are HR’s. Moments that bring you here First week. A missing document reminder. Policy acknowledgement. After HR adds a task. ⓘ Case on Employee Onboarding is a workflow on the Employee source. Templates live with HR, not in this self-service list. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open My onboarding] --> B[See assigned tasks] B --> C[Open a task] C --> D[Upload / acknowledge / form] D --> E[Save] E --> F[HR case status updates] 1 Open Workspace → My onboarding. 2 Pick a task Items hang off your onboarding case. 3 Complete Document, policy ack, or form. 4 HR sees it People → Onboarding is the operator view. Overview My onboarding is self-service on the employee’s onboarding case. HR still owns templates and the operator register under People → Onboarding. Employee remains the person record. How to use 1. Finish what is assigned You cannot invent extra case types here. 2. Documents follow rules Sensitive files are not for Work Graph snippets. 3. Blocked tasks Wait on HR or a prior step — do not open a parallel ticket unless asked. Related pages Onboarding (HR) Operator register. Policies Acknowledgements may point here. Employees The Employee row the case hangs on. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: My Paychecks
pages.description: Published payslips and paycheck history for your employment — only what payroll has already finalized.
headings: Your slips, after payroll says they exist
pages.content: My Paychecks — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → My paychecks Published pay Your slips, after payroll says they exist My paychecks shows finalized payslips for the signed-in employee. Nothing here creates a run or edits a salary structure. Workspace → My paychecks Route /workspace/my-paychecks Org flag myPaychecksEnabled Employee (self) The job of this console Find a period, open the slip, download if you need a copy. Corrections go through payroll operations, not this inbox. Seat at the table Employees with myPaychecksEnabled. Payroll managers use Paychecks and Runs under Payroll. The working rhythm Open after payday, pick the period, read the slip. Stop if the period is missing — it is not published yet. Moments that bring you here Payday. Tax document season. A deduction that looks wrong. After you changed a bank field on profile. ⓘ Published Paycheck rows Source is the payroll run that published the slip. Bank and salary remain on Employee with persona masking. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open My paychecks] --> B[Pick a period] B --> C[Open published slip] C --> D[Read / download PDF] D --> E{Question?} E -->|Yes| F[Ask payroll] E -->|No| G[Done] 1 Open Workspace → My paychecks. 2 Select period Only published runs appear. 3 View PDF or on-screen slip. 4 Escalate Payroll owns corrections. Overview My paychecks is self-service on published Paycheck rows from finalized payroll runs. It is not the payroll run console and not a place to change salary structures. How to use 1. Published only Draft and calculating runs stay on Payroll → Runs. 2. No line edits Wrong hours or leave must be fixed on timesheet/attendance, then a new run. 3. Masking You see your pay; you do not see the register of others. Related pages Paychecks (payroll) Org-wide published slips. Payroll runs Where slips are created. Payroll readiness Gates before a run. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: My Tickets
pages.description: Service tickets you opened or are assigned — the same ticket records the project service desk uses.
headings: Your tickets, still the desk’s records
pages.content: My Tickets — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → My tickets Personal service queue Your tickets, still the desk’s records My tickets shows service desk rows you requested or own. Status changes write to that ticket, not a private list. Workspace → My tickets Route /workspace/my-tickets Org flag myTicketsEnabled Employee · Assignee The job of this console Track what you opened, answer a waiting-on-you prompt, and close when the desk agrees. Raise new work on the team tickets screen if you have it. Seat at the table Employees and assignees with myTicketsEnabled. Service owners use Projects → Tickets & service. The working rhythm Filter mine, open, comment, save. Watch SLA on the ticket detail, not on this list alone. Moments that bring you here A laptop request that became a ticket. Waiting on you. After an SLA reminder. When chat said ‘I’ll ticket it’. ⓘ One ticket entity This is not a shadow helpdesk. Access grants may still need Admin access requests or Roles. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open My tickets] --> B[Filter mine] B --> C[Open ticket] C --> D[Comment / status] D --> E[Save] E --> F[Service desk register matches] 1 Open Workspace → My tickets. 2 Filter Requested by you vs assigned to you. 3 Update Status and comments on the ticket entity. 4 Confirm Team tickets register is the same row. Overview My tickets is a personal slice of the ticket / service desk entity. It is not a second helpdesk. Access requests for laptops still live under Admin access requests when that is the domain. How to use 1. Same ticket everywhere Do not recapture the issue in chat as the only copy. 2. SLA lives on the ticket This queue does not override policy. 3. Sensitive data No passwords or payroll files in comments. Related pages Tickets & service Team service desk. Access requests Elevated access / assets. Notifications Ticket events may land here. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: My Work
pages.description: Tasks, activities, and focus items assigned to you across projects — the same Task and TaskActivity rows delivery already uses.
headings: Your slice of the delivery chain
pages.content: My Work — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → My work Personal queue Your slice of the delivery chain My Work lists Task and TaskActivity assigned to you. Completing a row updates the project, not a private notebook. Workspace → My work Route /workspace/my-work Org flag myWorkEnabled Employee · Contributor · Manager The job of this console See what is due, open the item, move status, and comment. Create real delivery work on the project when something is missing from the queue. Seat at the table Anyone with assignments and myWorkEnabled. Managers still use project list and capacity for other people’s load. The working rhythm Filter, open, update, return. End the day with the queue, not a spreadsheet export as the plan. Moments that bring you here Monday planning. After standup. A ping that you own a blocked task. Before timesheet Friday — to know which activity to log. ⓘ Queue, not ledger Deliverable means Task. Work item means TaskActivity. My Work does not replace either table. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open My work] --> B[Filter status / project] B --> C[Open a row] C --> D[Update Task or TaskActivity] D --> E[Save] E --> F[Queue refreshes] 1 Open My work Workspace → My work. 2 Filter Status, project, due date. 3 Open Row is a Task or TaskActivity. 4 Update Status and comments write to delivery sources. Overview My Work is a personal queue over Task and TaskActivity assigned to you. It is not a personal kanban database. Hours still belong on Timesheet. How to use 1. Do not invent shadow tasks If work must be planned for the project, create it on the project’s deliverables, then it appears here. 2. Timesheet is elsewhere Logging hours is People → Timesheets, pointed at the same work item. 3. Pin filters, not copies Saved filters are convenience, not a second backlog. Related pages Workspace Home Launch pad. Task board Team flow on the same tasks. Work items TaskActivity grain. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Notifications
pages.description: Alerts, mentions, and system updates that deep-link to the record that changed — not a second inbox of work.
headings: Pings that already happened on a source record
pages.content: Notifications — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → Notifications Event list Pings that already happened on a source record Notifications are a reading surface on domain events. Opening one should land you on leave, a task, a ticket, or an approval — not on a message that is the only copy of the decision. Workspace → Notifications Route /workspace/notifications Org flag notificationsEnabled All signed-in personas The job of this console Clear unread, jump to the record, act there, mark read. Dismiss noise; do not rebuild work from the alert text. Seat at the table Everyone with notificationsEnabled. Admins still author templates. Workflows may generate the event. The working rhythm Open the center or bell, click through, finish on the source screen, return only for the next unread. Moments that bring you here After submit. A mention. SLA mail. When the bell is red and you do not know which module moved. ⓘ Events, not work items A notification never replaces Task, leave, or paycheck. Templates supply copy; sources supply truth. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Notifications] --> B[Scan unread] B --> C[Open an alert] C --> D[Land on source record] D --> E[Act there] E --> F[Mark read] 1 Open Workspace → Notifications or the bell. 2 Scan Unread project, approval, and mention items. 3 Jump Deep link opens the owning screen. 4 Act Approve, comment, or dismiss from the source. Overview The notification center lists events already written by leave, timesheet, tickets, workflows, and similar. Copy still comes from notification templates. Preferences live on profile. How to use 1. Jump, then act Do not treat the list as a todo database. 2. Templates own wording Bad subject lines are Admin → Notification templates. 3. Profile for channels Email vs in-app is not configured on this register. Related pages My approvals Decisions the alerts often point at. Notification templates Subject and body. Profile Notification preferences. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.

pages.title: Work Graph
pages.description: Connected operational truth across modules — nodes and edges that point at Employee, Project, Task, and similar sources, with masked snippets.
headings: Edges that point home, never a second HRIS
pages.content: Work Graph — Tracopus User Guide Home → Workspace → Work graph Relationship index Edges that point home, never a second HRIS Work Graph shows how Employee, Project, Task, PO, and tickets connect. Nodes are references; the file still lives on the source screen. Workspace → Work graph Route /workspace/work-graph Org flag workGraphEnabled Manager · Project Manager · Resource Manager · Executive · Admin The job of this console Find a person or project, see what hangs off them, and click through to edit. Use it for orientation, not for storing new facts in node text. Seat at the table Managers, resource, executives, and admins with workGraphEnabled. Employees typically do not get this map. The working rhythm Search, expand, open source, come back only if you need another neighbour. Moments that bring you here Who is on this PO’s projects. Why a ticket mentions a person. Before a reorg conversation. When search lists are too flat. ⓘ Masked summaries only Do not persist unmasked salary, bank, tax, document, medical, or performance values in graph metadata or search snippets. Flowcharts flowchart TD A[Open Work graph] --> B[Search a node] B --> C[Expand neighbours] C --> D[Open source screen] D --> E[Edit there if needed] E --> F[Graph refreshes from sources] 1 Open Workspace → Work graph. 2 Search Employee, project, ticket, PO. 3 Walk Edges are relationships, not new records. 4 Land Edit on the source console. Overview Work Graph is a relationship index over canonical entities. Search snippets and node metadata must stay masked for salary, bank, tax, medical, and performance-sensitive fields. How to use 1. Index, not master Create people and projects on their registers. 2. Masked snippets only Never persist raw sensitive values in graph metadata. 3. Analytics twin Work graph analytics is a charting lens on similar signals. Related pages Work graph analytics Charting lens. Employees People source. Project list Delivery source. © 2026 Tracopus . All rights reserved.
